# Introduction: Heterogeneous spatiotemporal GARCH model

This document provides the code required to reproduce the estimation, spatial prediction, and validation results for the heterogeneous spatiotemporal GARCH model. The model is designed for spatially indexed time series whose conditional variability changes both over time and across locations. Spatial heterogeneity is introduced through location-dependent GARCH coefficient functions, while contemporaneous spatial dependence is captured through the innovation field.

Let $Z_t(s)$ denote the process observed at time $t$ and location $s\in\mathcal D$. The STGARCH$(p,q)$ model is defined by
$$
Z_t(s)=\sigma_t(s)\eta_t(s),
$$
with conditional variance
$$
\sigma_t^2(s)
=
\omega(s)
+
\sum_{j=1}^{q}
\alpha_j(s)Z_{t-j}^2(s)
+
\sum_{i=1}^{p}
\beta_i(s)\sigma_{t-i}^2(s).
$$
The innovation field satisfies
$$
\mathbb E\{\eta_t(s)\}=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E\{\eta_t^2(s)\}=1,
$$
and is assumed to be independent over time but potentially dependent across space. The functions $\omega(s)$, $\alpha_j(s)$, and $\beta_i(s)$ allow the volatility dynamics to vary smoothly over the spatial domain.

The empirical implementation uses the STGARCH$(1,1)$ specification
$$
\sigma_t^2(s)
=
\omega(s)
+
\alpha(s)Z_{t-1}^2(s)
+
\beta(s)\sigma_{t-1}^2(s),
$$
subject to
$$
\omega(s)>0,
\qquad
\alpha(s)\geq0,
\qquad
\beta(s)\geq0,
\qquad
\alpha(s)+\beta(s)<1.
$$
The final condition ensures stability of the local conditional-variance recursion.

The spatially varying parameter vector
$$
\Theta(s)
=
\bigl\{
\omega(s),\alpha(s),\beta(s)
\bigr\}^{\top}
$$
is estimated locally. At a target location $s_0$, observations from surrounding locations receive kernel weights
$$
w_i(s_0)
=
K_b(s_i-s_0),
$$
where $K_b(\cdot)$ is a spatial kernel with bandwidth $b$. The local weighted quasi-maximum likelihood estimator is
$$
\widehat{\Theta}(s_0)
=
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\Theta}
\sum_{t=1}^{T}
\sum_{i=1}^{m}
w_i(s_0)
\left[
\log\{\sigma_t^2(s_i;\Theta)\}
+
\frac{Z_t^2(s_i)}
{\sigma_t^2(s_i;\Theta)}
\right].
$$
This local estimation strategy permits gradual spatial variation in the volatility dynamics without requiring a separate unrestricted time-series model at every location.

After estimating the local GARCH parameters, the standardized innovations are recovered as
$$
\widehat{\eta}_t(s_i)
=
\frac{Z_t(s_i)}
{\widehat{\sigma}_t(s_i)}.
$$
Their spatial covariance structure is then estimated and used to predict volatility at locations not employed in model fitting. Two spatial prediction strategies are considered. The first constructs a best linear predictor of the centered squared innovation
$$
\xi_t(s)=\eta_t^2(s)-1.
$$
The second assumes that $\eta_t(\cdot)$ is a Gaussian spatial process and uses the conditional-moment identity
$$
\mathbb E\!\left[
\eta_t^2(s_0)
\mid
\boldsymbol{\eta}_t
\right]
=
\mu_{\eta,t}^2(s_0)
+
v_\eta(s_0),
$$
where $\mu_{\eta,t}(s_0)$ and $v_\eta(s_0)$ are the conditional mean and variance obtained from Gaussian spatial prediction.

For either method, the predicted squared process is constructed recursively as
$$
\widehat{\sigma}_t^2(s_0)
=
\widehat{\omega}(s_0)
+
\widehat{\alpha}(s_0)
\widehat Z_{t-1}^2(s_0)
+
\widehat{\beta}(s_0)
\widehat{\sigma}_{t-1}^2(s_0),
$$
followed by
$$
\widehat Z_t^2(s_0)
=
\widehat{\sigma}_t^2(s_0)
\widehat{\eta_t^2}(s_0).
$$

The following sections implement this workflow, compare the two spatial predictors using identical cross-validation folds, and evaluate their predictive accuracy. Independent local estimation and prediction tasks are evaluated in parallel across spatial locations, while the time recursion within each location remains sequential.


# Functions needed for the code

```{r}
#| label: functions
#| message: false
#| eval: true
#| warning: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Functions used in the simulations and case studies"

# STGARCH(1,1): local QMLE and the two feasible predictors in Appendix C.
# Only complete, finite input data are supported. Preprocessing is external.
# Coordinates must be on the same two-dimensional scale used in the paper.
# The xi covariance below uses the working relation C_xi = 2 C_eta^2;
# that relation is an additional fourth-moment restriction, not distribution-free.

stgarch_bandwidth <- function(dx, dy) {
  sqrt(mean(c(stats::var(dx), stats::var(dy)))) * length(dx)^(-1 / 6)
}

# backward compatibility
default_bandwidth <- function(dx, dy) {
  coords <- cbind(dx, dy)
  sigma <- sqrt(mean(apply(coords, 2, var)))
  
  sigma * length(dx)^(-1 / 6)
}

# backward compatibility
a2d_sepgauss <- function(dx, dy, b) {
  log_weights <- -0.5 * (
    (dx / b)^2 +
      (dy / b)^2
  )
  
  weights <- exp(log_weights - max(log_weights))
  
  weights / sum(weights)
}

# backward compatibility
# Define uniform (box) kernels
a2d_box <- function(dx, dy, b) {
  # rectangular window: |dx| ≤ b and |dy| ≤ b
  w <- (abs(dx) <= b) & (abs(dy) <= b)
  w / sum(w)
}
# backward compatibility
# (optional circular window)
a2d_circle <- function(dx, dy, b) {
  d2 <- dx^2 + dy^2
  w <- (d2 <= b^2)
  w / sum(w)
}
# backward compatibility
# gaussian 
a2d_gaussian <- function(dx, dy, b) {
  
  d2 <- dx^2 + dy^2
  w  <- exp( - d2 / (2 * b^2) )
  w / sum(w)
}


# GARCH simulation given eta and params
simulation <- function(eta, omega, alpha, beta) {
  T <- nrow(eta);
  n <- ncol(eta)
  
  Z <- sigma2 <- matrix(0, nrow = T, ncol = n)
  
  # sigma2[1, ] <- omega
  sigma2[1, ] <- omega / (1 - alpha - beta)
  
  for (t in 2:T) {
    for (u in 1:n) {
      sigma2[t,u] <- omega[u] + alpha[u]*Z[t-1,u]^2 + beta[u]*sigma2[t-1,u]
      Z[t,u] <- sqrt(sigma2[t,u]) * eta[t,u]
    }
  }
  return(list(Z = Z, sigma2 = sigma2))
}




stgarch_weights <- function(dx, dy, b) {
  # A separable biweight kernel: symmetric, Lipschitz, and compactly supported,
  # as required by the theoretical kernel assumptions. Normalizing the weights
  # does not change the local QMLE minimizer.
  w <- pmax(1 - (dx / b)^2, 0)^2 * pmax(1 - (dy / b)^2, 0)^2
  if (sum(w) > 0) w / sum(w) else w
}

.stgarch_data <- function(Z, coords) {
  Z <- as.matrix(Z)
  coords <- as.matrix(coords)
  if (!is.numeric(Z) || !is.numeric(coords) || nrow(Z) < 3L ||
      ncol(Z) < 2L || nrow(coords) != ncol(Z) || ncol(coords) != 2L ||
      any(!is.finite(Z)) || any(!is.finite(coords)) ||
      any(!is.finite(Z^2))) {
    stop("Supply finite numeric Z (time x sites) and coords (sites x 2), ",
         "with at least three times and two sites.")
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(as.data.frame(coords)))
    stop("coords must identify distinct sites; duplicate coordinates need an explicit nugget interpretation.")
  list(Z = Z, coords = coords)
}

.stgarch_controls <- function(theta_init, lower, upper, stationarity_margin) {
  if (!is.numeric(theta_init) || !is.numeric(lower) || !is.numeric(upper) ||
      length(theta_init) != 3L || length(lower) != 3L || length(upper) != 3L ||
      any(!is.finite(c(theta_init, lower, upper))) ||
      lower[1] <= 0 || any(lower[2:3] < 0) || any(upper <= lower) ||
      length(stationarity_margin) != 1L || !is.finite(stationarity_margin) ||
      stationarity_margin <= 0 || stationarity_margin >= 1 ||
      any(theta_init <= lower) || any(theta_init >= upper) ||
      sum(theta_init[2:3]) >= 1 - stationarity_margin) {
    stop("Use finite bounds, lower[1] > 0, nonnegative alpha/beta bounds, ",
         "and an interior theta_init with alpha + beta < 1 - stationarity_margin.")
  }
}

.stgarch_parallel <- function(parallel, n_workers) {
  if (!is.logical(parallel) || length(parallel) != 1L || is.na(parallel))
    stop("parallel must be TRUE or FALSE.")
  if (!parallel) return(function() invisible(NULL))
  if (!requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE) ||
      !requireNamespace("future.apply", quietly = TRUE))
    stop("Install the future and future.apply packages for parallel fitting.")
  if (length(n_workers) != 1L || !is.finite(n_workers) ||
      n_workers < 2L || n_workers != as.integer(n_workers))
    stop("Use at least two integer workers when parallel = TRUE.")
  old_plan <- future::plan("list")
  # Separate R sessions work on Windows, macOS, and Linux, including RStudio.
  future::plan(future::multisession, workers = as.integer(n_workers))
  function() future::plan(old_plan)
}

.stgarch_map <- function(X, FUN, parallel) {
  if (parallel) {
    future.apply::future_lapply(X, FUN, future.seed = TRUE)
  } else {
    lapply(X, FUN)
  }
}

.stgarch_bandwidth <- function(coords, bandwidth, bandwidth_function) {
  if (is.null(bandwidth)) bandwidth <- bandwidth_function(coords[, 1], coords[, 2])
  if (length(bandwidth) != 1L || !is.finite(bandwidth) || bandwidth <= 0)
    stop("The bandwidth must be a finite positive scalar.")
  bandwidth
}

.stgarch_qml <- function(theta, Z2, w) {
  # The same unconditional initialization is used for fitting and inversion.
  # Row 1 initializes the recursion; rows 2:T enter the likelihood.
  omega <- theta[1]; alpha <- theta[2]; beta <- theta[3]
  gap <- 1 - alpha - beta
  if (omega <= 0 || alpha < 0 || beta < 0 || gap <= 0)
    return(list(value = Inf, gradient = rep(NA_real_, 3)))
  h <- rep(omega / gap, ncol(Z2))
  dh <- matrix(rep(c(1 / gap, omega / gap^2, omega / gap^2),
                   each = ncol(Z2)), ncol = 3L)
  value <- 0
  gradient <- numeric(3)
  for (tt in 2:nrow(Z2)) {
    dh <- cbind(1, Z2[tt - 1L, ], h) + beta * dh
    h <- omega + alpha * Z2[tt - 1L, ] + beta * h
    value <- value + sum(w * (log(h) + Z2[tt, ] / h)) / 2
    gradient <- gradient + colSums(dh * (w * (1 - Z2[tt, ] / h) / (2 * h)))
  }
  list(value = value / (nrow(Z2) - 1L),
       gradient = gradient / (nrow(Z2) - 1L))
}

.stgarch_local <- function(Z2, coords, target, theta_init, lower, upper,
                           bandwidth, weight_function, stationarity_margin) {
  w <- weight_function(coords[, 1] - target[1], coords[, 2] - target[2], bandwidth)
  if (length(w) != ncol(Z2) || any(!is.finite(w)) || any(w < 0) || sum(w) <= 0)
    stop("Invalid spatial weights or no sites inside the kernel support.")
  w <- w / sum(w)
  # Scaling changes the optimization coordinates, not the model or objective.
  scale <- c(max(sum(colMeans(Z2) * w), theta_init[1]), 1, 1)
  ui <- rbind(diag(3), -diag(3), c(0, -1, -1))
  ci <- c(lower, -upper, -(1 - stationarity_margin))
  ui <- sweep(ui, 2L, scale, `*`)
  last_x <- NULL; last_result <- NULL
  evaluate <- function(x) {
    if (!identical(x, last_x)) {
      last_result <<- .stgarch_qml(x * scale, Z2, w)
      last_x <<- x
    }
    last_result
  }
  fit <- stats::constrOptim(
    theta = theta_init / scale,
    f = function(x) evaluate(x)$value,
    grad = function(x) evaluate(x)$gradient * scale,
    ui = ui, ci = ci, method = "BFGS",
    control = list(maxit = 1000L, reltol = 1e-9),
    outer.iterations = 100L, outer.eps = 1e-7
  )
  theta <- fit$par * scale
  if (fit$convergence != 0L || !is.finite(fit$value) ||
      any(!is.finite(theta)) || any(theta < lower) || any(theta > upper) ||
      sum(theta[2:3]) > 1 - stationarity_margin)
    stop("Local QMLE failed at (", paste(signif(target, 6), collapse = ", "),
         "). Optimizer code: ", fit$convergence, ". No prediction was substituted.")
  stats::setNames(theta, c("omega", "alpha", "beta"))
}

stgarch_invert <- function(Z, parameters) {
  # parameters must correspond, in order, to the observed columns of Z.
  Z <- as.matrix(Z); 
  parameters <- as.matrix(parameters)
  if (!is.numeric(Z) || !is.numeric(parameters) || nrow(Z) < 2L ||
      nrow(parameters) != ncol(Z) || ncol(parameters) != 3L ||
      any(!is.finite(Z^2)) || any(!is.finite(parameters)) ||
      any(parameters[, 1] <= 0) || any(parameters[, 2:3] < 0) ||
      any(rowSums(parameters[, 2:3, drop = FALSE]) >= 1))
    stop("Invalid data or parameters for inversion.")
  h <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(Z), ncol(Z), dimnames = dimnames(Z))
  h[1, ] <- parameters[, 1] / (1 - parameters[, 2] - parameters[, 3])
  eta <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(Z), ncol(Z))
  for (tt in 2:nrow(Z)) {
    h[tt, ] <- parameters[, 1] + parameters[, 2] * Z[tt - 1L, ]^2 +
      parameters[, 3] * h[tt - 1L, ]
    eta[tt, ] <- Z[tt, ] / sqrt(h[tt, ])
  }
  if (any(!is.finite(h)) || any(!is.finite(eta[-1L, , drop = FALSE])))
    stop("Nonfinite variance or standardized residuals.")
  list(sigma2 = h, eta = eta, xi = eta^2 - 1)
}

.stgarch_covariance <- function(eta, D) {
  # Fit the exponential-plus-nugget model in (27) by Gaussian quasi-likelihood.
  # The free total variance is a nuisance scale; the fitted covariance is then
  # normalized to C_eta(0) = 1. Residual values are NOT rescaled or re-centered.
  positive_D <- D[D > 0]
  if (!length(positive_D)) stop("Spatial covariance requires distinct coordinates.")
  scale_D <- stats::median(positive_D)
  D_scaled <- D / scale_D
  S <- crossprod(eta) / nrow(eta)
  marginal <- mean(diag(S))
  if (!is.finite(marginal) || marginal <= 0) stop("Degenerate standardized residuals.")
  objective <- function(par) {
    R <- par[2] * exp(-D_scaled / par[1]) + diag(par[3], nrow(D))
    U <- tryCatch(chol(R), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(U)) return(.Machine$double.xmax / 100)
    inv_R <- chol2inv(U)
    sum(log(diag(U))) + sum(inv_R * S) / 2
  }
  fit <- stats::optim(
    par = c(1, 0.8 * marginal, 0.2 * marginal), fn = objective,
    method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = c(min(positive_D) / scale_D / 100, 1e-10, 1e-10),
    upper = c(2 * max(D_scaled), Inf, Inf),
    control = list(maxit = 1000L, factr = 1e7)
  )
  if (fit$convergence != 0L || !is.finite(fit$value) || any(!is.finite(fit$par)))
    stop("Spatial covariance fit failed; optimizer code: ", fit$convergence)
  range <- fit$par[1] * scale_D
  fraction <- fit$par[2] / sum(fit$par[2:3])
  R_eta <- fraction * exp(-D / range) + diag(1 - fraction, nrow(D))
  if (fit$par[1] <= min(positive_D) / scale_D / 100 * (1 + 1e-6) ||
      fit$par[1] >= 2 * max(D_scaled) * (1 - 1e-6))
    warning("Spatial range is at a search boundary; inspect covariance adequacy.")
  list(range = range, spatial_variance = fraction, nugget_variance = 1 - fraction,
       raw_total_variance = sum(fit$par[2:3]), R_eta = R_eta)
}

.stgarch_predict <- function(theta, eta, r_eta, R_chol, predictor, epsilon) {
  r <- if (predictor == "xi_blp") 2 * r_eta^2 else r_eta
  gamma <- as.numeric(backsolve(R_chol, forwardsolve(t(R_chol), r)))
  marginal <- if (predictor == "xi_blp") 2 else 1
  v <- marginal - sum(r * gamma)
  if (!is.finite(v) || v < -1e-8 * marginal)
    stop("Invalid kriging variance; check the covariance matrix and target covariance.")
  v <- max(v, 0) # Only remove negative roundoff; not a positivity adjustment.
  projection <- as.numeric(
    (if (predictor == "xi_blp") eta[-1L, , drop = FALSE]^2 - 1 else
      eta[-1L, , drop = FALSE]) %*% gamma
  )
  h <- z2 <- numeric(nrow(eta))
  spatial_mspe <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(eta))
  h[1] <- z2[1] <- theta[1] / (1 - theta[2] - theta[3])
  for (tt in 2:nrow(eta)) {
    h[tt] <- theta[1] + theta[2] * z2[tt - 1L] + theta[3] * h[tt - 1L]
    multiplier <- if (predictor == "xi_blp") 1 + projection[tt - 1L] else
      projection[tt - 1L]^2 + v
    raw <- h[tt] * multiplier
    if (!is.finite(h[tt]) || h[tt] <= 0 || !is.finite(raw))
      stop("Nonfinite prediction; no floor or fallback can repair this fit.")
    # Equation (35) truncates the PRODUCT, not the standardized multiplier.
    z2[tt] <- if (predictor == "xi_blp") max(raw, epsilon) else raw
    # (36) is for the unadjusted spatial error component, not total uncertainty.
    # Gaussian expression follows Var(eta_0^2 | eta) = 2 v^2 + 4 mu^2 v.
    spatial_mspe[tt] <- h[tt]^2 * if (predictor == "xi_blp") v else
      (2 * v^2 + 4 * projection[tt - 1L]^2 * v)
  }
  if (any(z2 < 0) || any(!is.finite(spatial_mspe[-1L])))
    stop("Invalid prediction or spatial error variance.")
  list(z2 = z2, h = h, spatial_mspe = spatial_mspe)
}

fit_stgarch_spatial_cv <- function(
    Z, coords, theta_init, lower, upper,
    predictor = c("xi_blp", "eta_gaussian"),
    folds = NULL, n_folds = 5L, seed = 5515L,
    weight_function = stgarch_weights, bandwidth_function = stgarch_bandwidth,
    bandwidth = NULL, stationarity_margin = 1e-4, epsilon = 1e-8,
    parallel = FALSE, n_workers = 2L, progress = interactive()) {
  predictor <- match.arg(predictor)
  input <- .stgarch_data(Z, coords); Z <- input$Z; coords <- input$coords
  .stgarch_controls(theta_init, lower, upper, stationarity_margin)
  if (length(epsilon) != 1L || !is.finite(epsilon) || epsilon <= 0)
    stop("epsilon must be finite and positive.")
  n <- ncol(Z)
  if (is.null(folds)) {
    if (length(n_folds) != 1L || !is.finite(n_folds) || n_folds < 2L ||
        n_folds > n || n_folds != as.integer(n_folds)) stop("Invalid n_folds.")
    # Preserve the caller's random-number state when generating folds.
    had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)
    if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv)
    set.seed(seed)
    folds <- sample(rep(seq_len(n_folds), length.out = n))
    if (had_seed) assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = .GlobalEnv) else
      rm(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv)
  }
  if (length(folds) != n || anyNA(folds) || length(unique(folds)) < 2L)
    stop("folds must assign every site to one of at least two folds.")
  bandwidth <- .stgarch_bandwidth(coords, bandwidth, bandwidth_function)
  restore <- .stgarch_parallel(parallel, n_workers); on.exit(restore(), add = TRUE)
  Z_pred_S2 <- sigma2_pred_S2 <- spatial_mspe <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(Z), n,
                                                        dimnames = dimnames(Z))
  parameters <- matrix(NA_real_, n, 3L,
                       dimnames = list(colnames(Z), c("omega", "alpha", "beta")))
  covariance_fits <- list()
  for (fold in unique(folds)) {
    if (progress) message("Fitting fold ", fold)
    test <- which(folds == fold); train <- which(folds != fold)
    if (length(train) < 2L) stop("Every fold needs at least two training sites.")
    Z_train <- Z[, train, drop = FALSE]
    coords_train <- coords[train, , drop = FALSE]
    local_fit <- function(target) .stgarch_local(
      Z_train^2, coords_train, target, theta_init, lower, upper,
      bandwidth, weight_function, stationarity_margin
    )
    training_parameters <- do.call(rbind, .stgarch_map(
      seq_along(train), function(j) local_fit(coords_train[j, ]), parallel
    ))
    eta <- stgarch_invert(Z_train, training_parameters)$eta
    D <- as.matrix(stats::dist(coords_train))
    cov_fit <- .stgarch_covariance(eta[-1L, , drop = FALSE], D)
    R <- if (predictor == "xi_blp") 2 * cov_fit$R_eta^2 else cov_fit$R_eta
    R_chol <- chol(R)
    predictions <- .stgarch_map(test, function(i) {
      theta <- local_fit(coords[i, ])
      distances <- sqrt(rowSums(sweep(coords_train, 2L, coords[i, ], `-`)^2))
      # No nugget in cross-covariance to a distinct, unobserved site.
      r_eta <- cov_fit$spatial_variance * exp(-distances / cov_fit$range)
      list(theta = theta, prediction = .stgarch_predict(
        theta, eta, r_eta, R_chol, predictor, epsilon
      ))
    }, parallel)
    for (j in seq_along(test)) {
      i <- test[j]; out <- predictions[[j]]
      parameters[i, ] <- out$theta
      Z_pred_S2[, i] <- out$prediction$z2
      sigma2_pred_S2[, i] <- out$prediction$h
      spatial_mspe[, i] <- out$prediction$spatial_mspe
    }
    cov_fit$R_eta <- NULL
    covariance_fits[[as.character(fold)]] <- cov_fit
  }
  # The empirical section defines the volatility score using sqrt(h), not
  # sqrt(predicted Z^2). These are different prediction targets. Absolute Z is
  # a noisy proxy, so this is not direct error against the latent true sigma.
  error <- sqrt(sigma2_pred_S2[-1L, , drop = FALSE]) - abs(Z[-1L, , drop = FALSE])
  if (any(!is.finite(error))) stop("Incomplete CV evaluation; refusing a partial score.")
  if (!is.finite(mean(error^2))) stop("Overflow in the CV score.")
  list(Z_pred_S2 = Z_pred_S2, sigma2_pred_S2 = sigma2_pred_S2,
       estimated_params = parameters, estimated_params_all = parameters,
       spatial_mspe = spatial_mspe, folds = folds, predictor = predictor,
       RMSE_vol = sqrt(mean(error^2)), MAE_vol = mean(abs(error)),
       evaluation_coverage = 1, bandwidth = bandwidth, covariance_fits = covariance_fits)
}

fit_stgarch_local_parameters <- function(
    Z, coords, theta_init, lower, upper, target_coords = coords,
    weight_function = stgarch_weights, bandwidth_function = stgarch_bandwidth,
    bandwidth = NULL, stationarity_margin = 1e-4,
    parallel = FALSE, n_workers = 2L, progress = interactive()) {
  input <- .stgarch_data(Z, coords); Z <- input$Z; coords <- input$coords
  .stgarch_controls(theta_init, lower, upper, stationarity_margin)
  target_coords <- as.matrix(target_coords)
  if (!is.numeric(target_coords) || ncol(target_coords) != 2L ||
      nrow(target_coords) < 1L || any(!is.finite(target_coords)))
    stop("target_coords must be a finite numeric matrix with two columns.")
  bandwidth <- .stgarch_bandwidth(coords, bandwidth, bandwidth_function)
  restore <- .stgarch_parallel(parallel, n_workers); on.exit(restore(), add = TRUE)
  if (progress) message("Fitting ", nrow(target_coords), " local parameter vectors")
  parameters <- do.call(rbind, .stgarch_map(seq_len(nrow(target_coords)), function(i) {
    .stgarch_local(Z^2, coords, target_coords[i, ], theta_init, lower, upper,
                   bandwidth, weight_function, stationarity_margin)
  }, parallel))
  list(estimated_params = parameters, estimated_params_all = parameters,
       target_coords = target_coords, bandwidth = bandwidth)
}


```

# Reduced Monte Carlo simulation

The following experiment illustrates the complete simulation, estimation and
prediction workflow. To keep the rendering time manageable, it uses ten Monte
Carlo replications. These settings are intended as a
computational demonstration rather than as a replacement for the full
simulation study reported in the paper.


```{r}
#| label: run-reduced-simulation
#| code-fold: false
#| code-summary: "Show simulation code"
#| cache: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

source("stgarch_spatial_estimation_parallelCV.R")


if (!exists("simulation", mode = "function")) {
  stop("First define or source the original simulation() function.")
}

if (!exists("a2d_box", mode = "function")) {
  stop("First define or source the original a2d_box() kernel function.")
}

# ==============================================================================
# Simulation design and estimation settings
# ==============================================================================

T <- 300L
p <- 1L
n1 <- 150L
n2 <- 50L
MC <- 10L

n_knots <- 4L
degree <- 3L
sigma2_eta <- 1
theta_range <- 0.5
grid_size <- 10L

parallel_sim <- TRUE
n_workers_sim <- 5L

predictors <- c("xi_blp", "eta_gaussian")

# Method used for the unsuffixed output aliases below.
predictor <- "xi_blp"

param_names <- c("omega", "alpha", "beta")

# Fixed finite bounds containing the simulated parameter surfaces.
theta_init <- c(omega = 0.3, alpha = 0.2, beta = 0.3)
lb <- c(omega = 1e-8, alpha = 0, beta = 0)
ub <- c(omega = 1, alpha = 1, beta = 1)

stationarity_margin <- 1e-4
epsilon <- 1e-8

# Retain the original bandwidth and box kernel.
b <- n1^(-1 / 4)
simulation_weights <- a2d_box

# Prediction grid.
x_vals <- seq(0, 1, length.out = grid_size)
y_vals <- seq(0, 1, length.out = grid_size)
grid <- expand.grid(x = x_vals, y = y_vals)
S0 <- as.matrix(grid)
n0 <- nrow(S0)

internal_knots <- seq(
  0, 1, length.out = n_knots + 2L
)[-c(1L, n_knots + 2L)]

# Row-wise tensor-product basis: one row per spatial location.
spatial_basis <- function(S) {

  Bx <- splines2::bSpline(
    S[, 1],
    knots = internal_knots,
    degree = degree,
    intercept = TRUE,
    Boundary.knots = c(0, 1)
  )

  By <- splines2::bSpline(
    S[, 2],
    knots = internal_knots,
    degree = degree,
    intercept = TRUE,
    Boundary.knots = c(0, 1)
  )

  do.call(
    cbind,
    lapply(seq_len(ncol(Bx)), function(j) {
      By * Bx[, j]
    })
  )
}

# ==============================================================================
# Storage
# ==============================================================================

new_prediction_array <- function() {
  array(NA_real_, dim = c(T, n2, MC))
}

estimated_params_S0_MC <- true_params_S0_MC <- array(
  NA_real_,
  dim = c(n0, 3L, MC),
  dimnames = list(NULL, param_names, NULL)
)

Z_true_S2_MC <- sigma2_true_S2_MC <- new_prediction_array()

Z_pred_by_method <- setNames(
  lapply(predictors, function(x) new_prediction_array()),
  predictors
)

sigma2_pred_by_method <- setNames(
  lapply(predictors, function(x) new_prediction_array()),
  predictors
)

pred_vol_S2_MC <- true_vol_S2_MC <- matrix(
  NA_real_, nrow = n2, ncol = MC
)

covariance_fits_MC <- vector("list", MC)
locations_MC <- vector("list", MC)

# ==============================================================================
# Monte Carlo replications
# ==============================================================================

for (mc_id in seq_len(MC)) {

  set.seed(mc_id)

  cat(sprintf(
    "Monte Carlo replication %d / %d\n",
    mc_id, MC
  ))

  S1 <- matrix(runif(n1 * 2L), ncol = 2L)
  S2 <- matrix(runif(n2 * 2L), ncol = 2L)

  locations_MC[[mc_id]] <- list(S1 = S1, S2 = S2)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # True parameter surfaces
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  B_S1 <- spatial_basis(S1)
  B_S2 <- spatial_basis(S2)
  B_S0 <- spatial_basis(S0)

  stopifnot(max(abs(rowSums(B_S0) - 1)) < 1e-10)

  nb <- ncol(B_S1)

  beta_omega <- 0.05 + 0.3 * runif(nb)
  beta_alpha <- 0.05 + 0.3 * runif(nb)
  beta_beta <- 0.05 + 0.5 * runif(nb)

  coefficients <- cbind(
    beta_omega,
    beta_alpha,
    beta_beta
  )

  true_params_S1 <- B_S1 %*% coefficients
  true_params_S2 <- B_S2 %*% coefficients
  true_params_S0 <- B_S0 %*% coefficients

  colnames(true_params_S1) <-
    colnames(true_params_S2) <-
    colnames(true_params_S0) <- param_names

  true_params_S0_MC[, , mc_id] <- true_params_S0

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Simulate spatially correlated Gaussian innovations and GARCH observations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  D_all <- as.matrix(
    stats::dist(rbind(S1, S2))
  )

  cov_eta <- sigma2_eta * exp(-D_all / theta_range)
  L <- t(chol(cov_eta))

  eta <- t(
    L %*% matrix(
      rnorm((n1 + n2) * T),
      nrow = n1 + n2
    )
  )

  sim1 <- simulation(
    eta[, seq_len(n1), drop = FALSE],
    true_params_S1[, "omega"],
    true_params_S1[, "alpha"],
    true_params_S1[, "beta"]
  )

  sim2 <- simulation(
    eta[, n1 + seq_len(n2), drop = FALSE],
    true_params_S2[, "omega"],
    true_params_S2[, "alpha"],
    true_params_S2[, "beta"]
  )

  Z_S1 <- as.matrix(sim1$Z)
  Z_S2 <- as.matrix(sim2$Z)
  sigma2_S1 <- as.matrix(sim1$sigma2)
  sigma2_S2 <- as.matrix(sim2$sigma2)

  stopifnot(
    identical(dim(Z_S1), c(T, n1)),
    identical(dim(Z_S2), c(T, n2)),
    identical(dim(sigma2_S1), c(T, n1)),
    identical(dim(sigma2_S2), c(T, n2)),
    all(is.finite(Z_S1)),
    all(is.finite(Z_S2)),
    all(is.finite(sigma2_S1)),
    all(is.finite(sigma2_S2)),
    all(sigma2_S1 > 0),
    all(sigma2_S2 > 0)
  )

  Z_true_S2_MC[, , mc_id] <- Z_S2
  sigma2_true_S2_MC[, , mc_id] <- sigma2_S2

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Local parameter estimation using S1 observations only
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # Fit parameters at training sites, prediction sites, and grid sites together.
  local_fit <- fit_stgarch_local_parameters(
    Z = Z_S1,
    coords = S1,
    target_coords = rbind(S1, S2, S0),
    theta_init = theta_init,
    lower = lb,
    upper = ub,
    weight_function = simulation_weights,
    bandwidth = b,
    stationarity_margin = stationarity_margin,
    parallel = parallel_sim,
    n_workers = n_workers_sim,
    progress = FALSE
  )

  estimated_params_S1 <- local_fit$estimated_params[
    seq_len(n1), , drop = FALSE
  ]

  estimated_params_S2 <- local_fit$estimated_params[
    n1 + seq_len(n2), , drop = FALSE
  ]

  estimated_params_S0 <- local_fit$estimated_params[
    n1 + n2 + seq_len(n0), , drop = FALSE
  ]

  estimated_params_S0_MC[, , mc_id] <- estimated_params_S0

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Recover innovations and fit their spatial covariance
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  inv <- stgarch_invert(
    Z_S1,
    estimated_params_S1
  )

  eta_S1_hat <- inv$eta
  xi_S1_hat <- inv$xi
  zeta_S1_hat <- inv$sigma2 * inv$xi

  D_train <- as.matrix(stats::dist(S1))

  # Same covariance helper used by fit_stgarch_spatial_cv().
  par_eta_hat <- .stgarch_covariance(
    eta_S1_hat[-1L, , drop = FALSE],
    D_train
  )

  covariance_fits_MC[[mc_id]] <- par_eta_hat[
    setdiff(names(par_eta_hat), "R_eta")
  ]

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Predict at S2 using both methods, without using S2 observations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  for (method in predictors) {

    R <- if (method == "xi_blp") {
      2 * par_eta_hat$R_eta^2
    } else {
      par_eta_hat$R_eta
    }

    R_chol <- chol(R)

    for (i in seq_len(n2)) {

      distances <- sqrt(
        rowSums(
          sweep(S1, 2L, S2[i, ], `-`)^2
        )
      )

      r_eta <- par_eta_hat$spatial_variance *
        exp(-distances / par_eta_hat$range)

      # Same prediction recursion used by fit_stgarch_spatial_cv().
      prediction <- .stgarch_predict(
        theta = estimated_params_S2[i, ],
        eta = eta_S1_hat,
        r_eta = r_eta,
        R_chol = R_chol,
        predictor = method,
        epsilon = epsilon
      )

      Z_pred_by_method[[method]][, i, mc_id] <-
        prediction$z2

      sigma2_pred_by_method[[method]][, i, mc_id] <-
        prediction$h
    }
  }

  # Unconditional standard deviations, not unconditional variances.
  pred_vol_S2_MC[, mc_id] <- sqrt(
    estimated_params_S2[, "omega"] /
      (
        1 - rowSums(
          estimated_params_S2[, c("alpha", "beta"), drop = FALSE]
        )
      )
  )

  true_vol_S2_MC[, mc_id] <- sqrt(
    true_params_S2[, "omega"] /
      (
        1 - rowSums(
          true_params_S2[, c("alpha", "beta"), drop = FALSE]
        )
      )
  )
}

# Convenient output names for subsequent chunks.
Z_pred_S2_MC <- Z_pred_by_method[[predictor]]
sigma2_pred_S2_MC <- sigma2_pred_by_method[[predictor]]

Z_pred_S2 <- Z_pred_S2_MC[, , MC]
sigma2_pred_S2 <- sigma2_pred_S2_MC[, , MC]

# ==============================================================================
# Scores against the known simulation truth
# ==============================================================================

score_error <- function(error) {

  stopifnot(all(is.finite(error)))

  c(
    Bias = mean(error),
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(error^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(error))
  )
}

# Exclude the initialization row.
# Unlike the empirical score against absolute observed returns, these scores
# evaluate predictions against the true latent conditional volatility.
dynamic_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(predictors, function(method) {

    do.call(
      rbind,
      lapply(seq_len(MC), function(mc_id) {

        error <- sqrt(
          sigma2_pred_by_method[[method]][-1L, , mc_id]
        ) - sqrt(
          sigma2_true_S2_MC[-1L, , mc_id]
        )

        data.frame(
          replication = mc_id,
          predictor = method,
          as.list(score_error(error)),
          row.names = NULL
        )
      })
    )
  })
)

print(dynamic_results)

# Parameter errors at the fixed S0 grid.
parameter_error <- estimated_params_S0_MC - true_params_S0_MC

bias_params_S0 <- apply(
  parameter_error, c(1, 2), mean
)

rmse_params_S0 <- sqrt(
  apply(parameter_error^2, c(1, 2), mean)
)

mae_params_S0 <- apply(
  abs(parameter_error), c(1, 2), mean
)

bias_omega_grid <- matrix(
  bias_params_S0[, "omega"], grid_size, grid_size
)

rmse_omega_grid <- matrix(
  rmse_params_S0[, "omega"], grid_size, grid_size
)

mae_omega_grid <- matrix(
  mae_params_S0[, "omega"], grid_size, grid_size
)

# Pool squared errors before taking the square root.
parameter_summary <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(param_names, function(param) {
    data.frame(
      parameter = param,
      as.list(score_error(parameter_error[, param, ]))
    )
  })
)

print(parameter_summary)

# S2 locations are redrawn in every replication: report pooled random-site errors.
unconditional_volatility_summary <- as.data.frame(
  as.list(
    score_error(pred_vol_S2_MC - true_vol_S2_MC)
  )
)

print(unconditional_volatility_summary)

# ==============================================================================
# Illustrations from the final replication
# ==============================================================================

plot_rep <- MC

pred_params_S0 <- estimated_params_S0_MC[, , plot_rep]
t_true_params_S0 <- true_params_S0_MC[, , plot_rep]

pred_vol_S0 <- sqrt(
  pred_params_S0[, "omega"] /
    (
      1 - rowSums(
        pred_params_S0[, c("alpha", "beta"), drop = FALSE]

)

true_vol_S0 <- sqrt(
  t_true_params_S0[, "omega"] /
    (
      1 - rowSums(
        t_true_params_S0[, c("alpha", "beta"), drop = FALSE]
      )
    )
)

pred_vol_S0_grid <- matrix(
  pred_vol_S0, grid_size, grid_size
)

true_vol_S0_grid <- matrix(
  true_vol_S0, grid_size, grid_size
)

image(
  x_vals, y_vals, pred_vol_S0_grid,
  col = heat.colors(100),
  xlab = "X",

contour_levels <- pretty(

contour(

local({
```

# Empirical applications

We illustrate the flexibility of the heterogeneous STGARCH model through two applications in distinct spatial settings. The first examines residual volatility in daily PM$_{10}$ concentrations across an irregular network of monitoring stations in Italy, where location is defined geographically and volatility represents time-varying model uncertainty. The second studies daily stock returns in a financial network, where firms are embedded in a latent economic space constructed from balance-sheet characteristics. Together, the applications demonstrate how the model can estimate spatially heterogeneous volatility dynamics and predict volatility at locations or firms excluded from model estimation.

## Financial network application

The financial application considers daily log returns for 50 publicly traded firms observed over 276 trading days in 2019. Because no physical coordinates or directly observed network are available, the firms are embedded in two-dimensional proxy spaces constructed from standardized balance-sheet variables. After preprocessing, 44 financial features remain, yielding 946 possible pairwise proxy spaces. For each space, predictive performance is evaluated by five-fold cross-validation, with the complete return history of each test firm withheld and its volatility predicted from economically similar training firms. The same fold assignments are used throughout, allowing the candidate proxy spaces and the two spatial prediction methods to be compared on a common basis.

### Financial data preprocessing

The preprocessing follows Fülle and Otto (2024). The code below preserves the computational steps of the original implementation; only unused diagnostic commands have been removed and the formatting and documentation have been standardised.

Fülle, M. J., & Otto, P. (2024). Spatial GARCH models for unknown spatial locations–an application to financial stock returns. Spatial Economic Analysis, 19(1), 92-105.

```{r}
#| label: financial-data-preprocessing
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show full code for data pre-processing"

# Required packages
library(xts)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

# Load the financial statements and stock-price series.
load("Finance_example/workspace.RData")


# ==============================================================================
# Balance-sheet covariates
# ==============================================================================

# Convert the financial data to a numeric matrix.
A <- data.matrix(financials)

# The data contain alternating annual observations. The odd-numbered rows
# correspond to the observations used for 2019.
row_index <- seq_len(nrow(A))
row_index <- row_index[row_index %% 2L != 0L]

A_2019 <- A[row_index, ]

# Retain the 66 balance-sheet variables used in the empirical analysis.
A_2019 <- A_2019[, 2:68]
A_2019 <- A_2019[, c(1:60, 62:67)]

# Harmonise the units of firms whose financial variables are reported on a
# scale differing by a factor of 1,000. These corrections reproduce the
# preprocessing of the original dataset.
A_2019["Samsung_Electronics", ] <-
  A_2019["Samsung_Electronics", ] / 1000

A_2019[18, ] <- A_2019[18, ] / 1000
A_2019[30, ] <- A_2019[30, ] / 1000
A_2019[47, ] <- A_2019[47, ] / 1000
A_2019[27, ] <- A_2019[27, ] / 1000
A_2019[23, ] <- A_2019[23, ] / 1000
A_2019[12, ] <- A_2019[12, ] / 1000
A_2019[8, ]  <- A_2019[8, ] / 1000
A_2019[7, ]  <- A_2019[7, ] / 1000

# Standardise each covariate across firms.
A_stand <- apply(
  A_2019,
  MARGIN = 2,
  FUN = function(x) {
    (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
)

# Missing standardised values are replaced by zero, corresponding to the
# cross-sectional mean of the respective covariate.
A_stand[is.na(A_stand)] <- 0
A_stand <- as.matrix(A_stand)


# ==============================================================================
# Stock-price series
# ==============================================================================

# Extract the price series for the 50 firms. Five observations are removed from
# the BNP Paribas series to reproduce the alignment used in the original data.
stock_list <- list(
  Allianz = Allianz[, 1],

  ATT = ATT[, 1],
  Santander = Banco_Santander[, 1],
  BofA = Bank_of_America[, 1],
  BHP = BHP_Billiton[, 1],
  BNP = BNP_Paribas[-c(111, 194, 252, 253, 256), 1],
  BP = BP[, 1],
  Chevron = Chevron[, 1],
  Cisco = Cisco[, 1],
  Citi = Citigroup[, 1],
  CocaCola = Coca_Cola[, 1],
  Conoco = ConocoPhillips[, 1],
  EON = E.ON[, 1],
  Eni = Eni[, 1],
  Exxon = Exxon_Mobil[, 1],
  Gazprom = Gazprom[, 1],
  GE = General_Electric[, 1],
  GSK = GlaxoSmithKline[, 1],
  Google = Google[, 1],
  HP = Hewlett_Packard[, 1],
  HSBC = HSBC[, 1],
  IBM = IBM[, 1],
  Intel = Intel[, 1],
  JnJ = Johnson_Johnson[, 1],
  JPM = JPMorgan_Chase_Co.[, 1],
  Merck = Merck_Co_Inc.[, 1],
  Microsoft = Microsoft[, 1],
  MUFG = Mitsubishi_UFJ_Financial_Group[, 1],
  Nestle = Nestlé[, 1],
  Novartis = Novartis[, 1],
  Oracle = Oracle[, 1],
  Pepsi = PepsiCo[, 1],
  Petrobras = Petrobras[, 1],
  Pfizer = Pfizer[, 1],
  PMI = Philip_Morris_International[, 1],
  PG = Procter_Gamble[, 1],
  Roche = Roche[, 1],
  Shell = Royal_Dutch_Shell[, 1],
  Samsung = Samsung_Electronics[, 1],
  Sanofi = Sanofi_Aventis[, 1],
  Schlumberger = Schlumberger[, 1],
  Siemens = Siemens[, 1],
  Telefonica = Telefónica[, 1],
  Total = Total[, 1],
  Toyota = Toyota[, 1],
  Verizon = Verizon_Communications[, 1],
  Vodafone = Vodafone_Group[, 1],
  Walmart = Wal_Mart[, 1]
)

# Preserve the date index used in the original analysis.
Dates <- zoo::index(Allianz)


# ==============================================================================
# Daily log-returns
# ==============================================================================

# Compute continuously compounded daily returns for each firm.
log_returns_list <- lapply(
  stock_list,
  function(prices) {
    prices <- as.numeric(prices)

    if (length(prices) >= 2L) {
      diff(log(prices))
    } else {
      NULL
    }
  }
)

# Combine the firm-specific return series in long format. Series are aligned by
# their sequential observation index, as in the original implementation.
panel_returns <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    names(log_returns_list),
    function(firm_name) {
      firm_returns <- log_returns_list[[firm_name]]

      if (!is.null(firm_returns)) {
        data.frame(
          firm = firm_name,
          time = seq_along(firm_returns),
          return = firm_returns
        )
      } else {
        NULL
      }
    }
  )
)

# Convert the return panel to wide format, with one column per firm.
panel_wide <- tidyr::pivot_wider(
  data = panel_returns,
  names_from = firm,
  values_from = return
)


# ==============================================================================
# Exploratory plot
# ==============================================================================

# Convert the return panel back to long format for plotting.
panel_long_plot <- panel_wide %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -time,
    names_to = "firm",
    values_to = "return"
  )

# Display the first nine firms in alphabetical order.
firms_to_plot <- sort(unique(panel_long_plot$firm))[1:9]

panel_long_plot_subset <- dplyr::filter(
  panel_long_plot,
  firm %in% firms_to_plot
)

ggplot(
  panel_long_plot_subset,
  aes(
    x = time,
    y = return,
    colour = firm
  )
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ firm,
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 3
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily log-returns for selected firms",
    x = "Time index (days)",
    y = "Log-return",
    colour = "Firm"
  )


# ==============================================================================
# Return matrix used for model estimation
# ==============================================================================

logreturns <- as.matrix(panel_wide[, -1])

# Series of unequal length generate a small number of missing observations.
# Following the original implementation, these values are replaced by draws
# from a centred Gaussian distribution with standard deviation 0.001.
#
# This step is stochastic. Exact replication requires the random seed used for
# the original analysis to be set before this command.
logreturns[is.na(logreturns)] <- rnorm(
  n = sum(is.na(logreturns)),
  mean = 0,
  sd = 0.001
)
```

### Selection of the financial proxy space

All pairs of balance-sheet variables with less than 5% missingness are considered as candidate two-dimensional proxy spaces. For each space, predictive performance is evaluated using the same five-fold cross-validation partition. The folds leave out complete firm-level time series. Spatially varying GARCH parameters are estimated from the training firms, and the squared process is predicted at the held-out firms by kriging the estimated innovation process.

The exhaustive search considers all admissible covariate pairs and is computationally intensive. The full code is provided below for reproducibility. The subsequent chunk loads the corresponding pre-computed results.


```{r}
#| label: financial-proxy-space-selection
#| eval: false
#| message: true
#| warning: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show financial proxy-space cross-validation"

source("stgarch_spatial_estimation_parallelCV.R")

if (!requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE) ||
    !requireNamespace("future.apply", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Install future and future.apply before running this block.")
}

logreturns <- as.matrix(logreturns)
A_stand <- as.matrix(A_stand)
n <- ncol(logreturns)
T <- nrow(logreturns)

if (!is.numeric(logreturns) || !is.numeric(A_stand) ||
    nrow(A_stand) != n || n < 5L || T < 3L ||
    any(!is.finite(logreturns^2)) || any(!is.finite(A_stand))) {
  stop("Supply finite logreturns (times x firms) and A_stand (firms x covariates), ",
       "with corresponding firm order and at least five firms.")
}

finance_lb <- c(omega = 1e-12, alpha = 0, beta = 0)
finance_ub <- c(omega = 1, alpha = 1, beta = 1)
finance_theta_init <- c(omega = 1e-5, alpha = 0.05, beta = 0.90)

# ==============================================================================
# Candidate two-dimensional financial proxy spaces
# ==============================================================================

# Retain the original zero-based filtering rule. It measures missingness only
# if the preprocessing used zeros exclusively to mark imputed missing values.
zero_proportion <- colMeans(A_stand == 0)
candidate_indices <- which(zero_proportion < 0.05)
if (length(candidate_indices) < 2L) {
  stop("Fewer than two covariates remain after filtering.")
}

# Preserve the original ordering of pair indices for downstream code.
pairs <- expand.grid(i = candidate_indices, j = candidate_indices)
pairs <- pairs[pairs$i < pairs$j, , drop = FALSE]
rownames(pairs) <- NULL

covariate_names <- colnames(A_stand)
if (is.null(covariate_names)) {
  covariate_names <- paste0("V", seq_len(ncol(A_stand)))
}

# ==============================================================================
# Identical folds for every proxy space and both predictors
# ==============================================================================

n_folds <- 5L
seed <- 5515L
set.seed(seed)
folds <- rep(seq_len(n_folds), length.out = n)[sample(seq_len(n))]

common_arguments <- list(
  Z = logreturns,
  theta_init = finance_theta_init,
  lower = finance_lb,
  upper = finance_ub,
  weight_function = a2d_sepgauss,
  bandwidth_function = default_bandwidth,
  stationarity_margin = 1e-4,
  epsilon = 1e-8,
  folds = folds,
  # Parallelize across proxy spaces, not within a proxy-space fit.
  parallel = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)

# ==============================================================================
# Compact results: retain both squared-process and variance predictions
# ==============================================================================

failed_fit <- function(message, bandwidth = NA_real_, warnings = character()) {
  list(
    Z_pred_S2 = NULL,
    sigma2_pred_S2 = NULL,
    RMSE_vol = NA_real_,
    MAE_vol = NA_real_,
    evaluation_coverage = 0,
    bandwidth = bandwidth,
    covariance_fits = list(),
    error = message,
    warnings = warnings
  )
}

compact_fit <- function(fit, warnings) {
  list(
    Z_pred_S2 = fit$Z_pred_S2,
    sigma2_pred_S2 = fit$sigma2_pred_S2,
    RMSE_vol = fit$RMSE_vol,
    MAE_vol = fit$MAE_vol,
    evaluation_coverage = fit$evaluation_coverage,
    bandwidth = fit$bandwidth,
    covariance_fits = fit$covariance_fits,
    error = NA_character_,
    warnings = warnings
  )
}

fit_one_proxy_space <- function(pair_index) {
  indices <- c(pairs$i[pair_index], pairs$j[pair_index])
  coords_pair <- A_stand[, indices, drop = FALSE]
  b_pair <- NA_real_

  design_error <- tryCatch({
    if (anyDuplicated(as.data.frame(coords_pair))) {
      stop("Duplicate firm coordinates: the current nugget model requires distinct sites.")
    }
    if (qr(cbind(1, coords_pair))$rank < 3L) {
      stop("The candidate coordinates do not span a two-dimensional space.")
    }
    b_pair <- common_arguments$bandwidth_function(coords_pair[, 1], coords_pair[, 2])
    if (length(b_pair) != 1L || !is.finite(b_pair) || b_pair <= 0) {
      stop("Invalid bandwidth for this proxy space.")
    }
    supported <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
      train <- folds != folds[i]
      w <- common_arguments$weight_function(
        coords_pair[train, 1] - coords_pair[i, 1],
        coords_pair[train, 2] - coords_pair[i, 2],
        b_pair
      )
      any(w > 0)
    }, logical(1))
    if (!all(supported)) {
      stop(sum(!supported), " held-out firms have no training kernel support ",
           "at bandwidth ", signif(b_pair, 5), ". Firm indices: ",
           paste(which(!supported), collapse = ", "))
    }
    NULL
  }, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))

  if (!is.null(design_error)) {
    return(list(pair_index = pair_index,
                xi_blp = failed_fit(design_error, b_pair),
                eta_gaussian = failed_fit(design_error, b_pair)))
  }

  run_predictor <- function(predictor_name) {
    fit_warnings <- character()
    tryCatch({
      fit <- withCallingHandlers(
        do.call(
          fit_stgarch_spatial_cv,
          c(common_arguments, list(coords = coords_pair,
                                   bandwidth = b_pair,
                                   predictor = predictor_name))
        ),
        warning = function(w) {
          fit_warnings <<- unique(c(fit_warnings, conditionMessage(w)))
          invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
        }
      )
      compact_fit(fit, fit_warnings)
    }, error = function(e) failed_fit(conditionMessage(e), b_pair, fit_warnings))
  }

  list(pair_index = pair_index,
       xi_blp = run_predictor("xi_blp"),
       eta_gaussian = run_predictor("eta_gaussian"))
}

# ==============================================================================
# Parallel search with restoration of the previous future plan
# ==============================================================================

## for testing:
pairs <- pairs[1:5, ]


n_workers <- 5L
previous_plan <- future::plan("list")
pair_results <- tryCatch({
  future::plan(future::multisession, workers = n_workers)
  future.apply::future_lapply(
    seq_len(nrow(pairs)), fit_one_proxy_space,
    future.seed = seed, future.globals = TRUE, future.scheduling = 2
  )
}, finally = future::plan(previous_plan))

output_xi <- lapply(pair_results, `[[`, "xi_blp")
output_eta <- lapply(pair_results, `[[`, "eta_gaussian")

RMSE_xi <- vapply(output_xi, `[[`, numeric(1), "RMSE_vol")
RMSE_eta <- vapply(output_eta, `[[`, numeric(1), "RMSE_vol")
MAE_xi <- vapply(output_xi, `[[`, numeric(1), "MAE_vol")
MAE_eta <- vapply(output_eta, `[[`, numeric(1), "MAE_vol")
coverage_xi <- vapply(output_xi, `[[`, numeric(1), "evaluation_coverage")
coverage_eta <- vapply(output_eta, `[[`, numeric(1), "evaluation_coverage")

comparison_rows <- function(results, predictor) {
  data.frame(
    pair_index = seq_len(nrow(pairs)),
    covariate_1_index = pairs$i,
    covariate_2_index = pairs$j,
    covariate_1 = covariate_names[pairs$i],
    covariate_2 = covariate_names[pairs$j],
    predictor = predictor,
    RMSE = vapply(results, `[[`, numeric(1), "RMSE_vol"),
    MAE = vapply(results, `[[`, numeric(1), "MAE_vol"),
    coverage = vapply(results, `[[`, numeric(1), "evaluation_coverage"),
    bandwidth = vapply(results, `[[`, numeric(1), "bandwidth"),
    error = vapply(results, `[[`, character(1), "error"),
    warnings = vapply(results, function(x) paste(x$warnings, collapse = " | "), character(1)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

proxy_space_comparison <- rbind(
  comparison_rows(output_xi, "xi_blp"),
  comparison_rows(output_eta, "eta_gaussian")
)
rownames(proxy_space_comparison) <- NULL
proxy_space_comparison$eligible <- with(
  proxy_space_comparison,
  is.na(error) & coverage == 1 & is.finite(RMSE) & is.finite(MAE)
)

# Rank only complete, successful evaluations, separately for each method.
# Recorded covariance warnings should still be reviewed before interpretation.
ranked_proxy_spaces <- proxy_space_comparison[proxy_space_comparison$eligible, ]
ranked_proxy_spaces <- ranked_proxy_spaces[
  order(ranked_proxy_spaces$predictor, ranked_proxy_spaces$RMSE),
  , drop = FALSE
]

# Compatibility aliases for downstream code using xi-BLP as the primary method.
RMSE <- RMSE_xi
output <- output_xi

# ==============================================================================
# Save results, including failures and the exact settings used
# ==============================================================================

financial_results_file <- file.path("Finance_example", "financial_proxy_space_CV_results.rds")
dir.create(dirname(financial_results_file), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

saveRDS(
  list(
    pairs = pairs, folds = folds, zero_proportion = zero_proportion,
    covariate_names = covariate_names,
    proxy_space_comparison = proxy_space_comparison,
    ranked_proxy_spaces = ranked_proxy_spaces,
    output_xi = output_xi, output_eta = output_eta,
    RMSE_xi = RMSE_xi, RMSE_eta = RMSE_eta,
    MAE_xi = MAE_xi, MAE_eta = MAE_eta,
    coverage_xi = coverage_xi, coverage_eta = coverage_eta,
    settings = list(
      theta_init = finance_theta_init, lower = finance_lb, upper = finance_ub,
      stationarity_margin = common_arguments$stationarity_margin,
      epsilon = common_arguments$epsilon,
      kernel = "separable Gaussian", bandwidth_rule = "default_bandwidth",
      score = "sqrt(sigma2_pred_S2) versus abs(logreturns), rows 2:T",
      n_folds = n_folds, seed = seed, n_workers = n_workers
    )
  ),
  file = financial_results_file,
  compress = "xz"
)

print(with(proxy_space_comparison, table(predictor, eligible)))
print(utils::head(ranked_proxy_spaces[ranked_proxy_spaces$predictor == "xi_blp", ], 5L))
print(utils::head(ranked_proxy_spaces[ranked_proxy_spaces$predictor == "eta_gaussian", ], 5L))

if (any(nzchar(proxy_space_comparison$warnings))) {
  warning("Some fits issued covariance warnings; review the saved warnings column.")
}
if (any(!proxy_space_comparison$eligible)) {
  warning("Some candidate-method combinations failed and were excluded from ranking. ",
          "See the saved error column; no partial-data RMSE was used.")
}
if (!nrow(ranked_proxy_spaces)) {
  stop("No candidate yielded a complete CV result. Diagnostics were saved to ",
       financial_results_file, ". Review kernel support, bounds, and fit errors.")
}



```

```{r}
if (!file.exists(financial_results_file)) {

# Candidate spaces, common folds, and estimation settings.

covariate_names <- financial_results$covariate_names

# Predictions and scores for both methods.

output_eta <- financial_results$output_eta

RMSE_eta <- financial_results$RMSE_eta

coverage_eta <- financial_results$coverage_eta
```

### Identify the relevant proxy spaces

The best-performing proxy space is used for the cross-validated volatility
predictions. The space, defined by other current liabilities and
long-term debt, is used for the detailed parameter-surface analysis because it
has a clearer economic interpretation.

```{r}
#| label: identify-financial-proxy-spaces
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Use the names saved with the CV results, not a potentially changed A_stand.
if (
  is.null(covariate_names) ||
  length(covariate_names) < max(c(pairs$i, pairs$j))
) {
  stop("The saved covariate names are missing or inconsistent with pairs.")
}

pair_summary <- data.frame(
  model_id = seq_len(nrow(pairs)),
  variable_1 = covariate_names[as.integer(pairs$i)],
  variable_2 = covariate_names[as.integer(pairs$j)],
  RMSE = RMSE,
  MAE = MAE,
  coverage = coverage,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

pair_summary$eligible <- with(
  pair_summary,
  is.finite(RMSE) &
    is.finite(MAE) &
    !is.na(coverage) &
    coverage == 1
)

# Return the model ID, irrespective of variable order or table row order.
find_pair_id <- function(variable_1, variable_2, pair_table) {
  matching_rows <- which(
    (
      pair_table$variable_1 == variable_1 &
        pair_table$variable_2 == variable_2
    ) |
      (
        pair_table$variable_1 == variable_2 &
          pair_table$variable_2 == variable_1
      )
  )

  if (length(matching_rows) != 1L) {
    stop(
      "Could not identify a unique proxy space for `",
      variable_1, "` and `", variable_2, "`."
    )
  }

  pair_table$model_id[matching_rows]
}

# Rank only complete, successful candidate evaluations.
ranked_rows <- which(pair_summary$eligible)

if (!length(ranked_rows)) {
  stop("No eligible proxy spaces are available for the selected predictor.")
}

ranked_rows <- ranked_rows[
  order(pair_summary$RMSE[ranked_rows])
]

best_id <- pair_summary$model_id[ranked_rows[1L]]

# Preserve this variable name for subsequent code.
top5_idx <- pair_summary$model_id[
  head(ranked_rows, 5L)
]

if (!pair_summary$eligible[best_id]) {
  stop(
    "The selected proxy space does not have a complete, valid CV result ",
    "for ", predictor, ". Inspect proxy_space_comparison$error."
  )
}

# Table of the best-performing candidates.
# The explicitly selected space need not belong to this top-five table.
proxy_space_results <- pair_summary[
  match(top5_idx, pair_summary$model_id),
  c("model_id", "variable_1", "variable_2", "RMSE"),
  drop = FALSE
]

method_label <- switch(
  predictor,
  xi_blp = "squared-innovation BLP",
  eta_gaussian = "Gaussian conditional-moment predictor"
)

knitr::kable(
  proxy_space_results,
  digits = 5,
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = paste0(
    "Best-performing financial proxy spaces using the ",
    method_label,
    "."
  )
)
```

### Variables recurring among the best proxy spaces

Figure 4 shows how frequently each balance-sheet variable occurs among the 30
best-performing proxy spaces and displays the corresponding undirected network.

```{r}
#| label: fig-top-proxy-space-network
#| fig-width: 13.5
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Variable frequencies and co-occurrence among up to 30 best-performing eligible proxy spaces for the selected predictor. Thicker edges indicate better CV-RMSE ranks."
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Select up to 30 eligible proxy spaces for the currently selected predictor.
top_k <- 30L

eligible_rows <- which(pair_summary$eligible)

eligible_rows <- eligible_rows[
  order(pair_summary$RMSE[eligible_rows])
]

top_rows <- head(eligible_rows, top_k)

if (!length(top_rows)) {
  stop("No eligible proxy spaces are available for this figure.")
}

top_ids <- pair_summary$model_id[top_rows]
top_pairs <- pairs[top_ids, , drop = FALSE]
top_rmse <- pair_summary$RMSE[top_rows]

# Use the actual number selected in all labels and calculations.
top_k <- length(top_ids)

# Use the covariate names saved with the estimation results.
variable_names <- covariate_names

if (
  is.null(variable_names) ||
  length(variable_names) < max(c(top_pairs$i, top_pairs$j))
) {
  stop("The saved covariate names are missing or inconsistent with pairs.")
}

# Count variable occurrences among the selected pairs.
top_variable_ids <- c(
  as.integer(top_pairs$i),
  as.integer(top_pairs$j)
)

variable_frequency <- sort(
  table(variable_names[top_variable_ids]),
  decreasing = TRUE
)

# Assign consistent short labels for both panels.
variable_labels <- if (length(variable_frequency) <= length(LETTERS)) {
  LETTERS[seq_along(variable_frequency)]
} else {
  paste0("V", seq_along(variable_frequency))
}

names(variable_labels) <- names(variable_frequency)

# Construct the network: each edge represents a selected variable pair.
edge_data <- data.frame(
  from = variable_names[as.integer(top_pairs$i)],
  to = variable_names[as.integer(top_pairs$j)],
  rank = seq_len(top_k),
  RMSE = top_rmse,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Better-ranked proxy spaces receive larger edge weights.
edge_data$weight <- rev(seq_len(top_k))

edge_data_aggregated <- aggregate(
  weight ~ from + to,
  data = edge_data,
  FUN = sum
)

proxy_graph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
  edge_data_aggregated,
  directed = FALSE
)

vertex_frequency <- table(
  c(edge_data$from, edge_data$to)
)

igraph::V(proxy_graph)$frequency <- as.numeric(
  vertex_frequency[igraph::V(proxy_graph)$name]
)

igraph::V(proxy_graph)$label <- unname(
  variable_labels[igraph::V(proxy_graph)$name]
)

igraph::V(proxy_graph)$size_scaled <-
  8 + 2.8 * igraph::V(proxy_graph)$frequency

# Scale edge widths safely, including single-edge or equal-weight cases.
edge_weight <- igraph::E(proxy_graph)$weight
weight_range <- range(edge_weight)

if (
  length(edge_weight) > 1L &&
  diff(weight_range) > 0
) {
  igraph::E(proxy_graph)$width_scaled <-
    0.8 + 3.2 *
      (edge_weight - weight_range[1]) /
      diff(weight_range)
} else {
  igraph::E(proxy_graph)$width_scaled <- rep(
    2,
    length(edge_weight)
  )
}

# Restore graphical settings even if plotting fails.
local({
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)

  on.exit({
    layout(1)
    par(old_par)
  })
  
  # pdf("proxy_space_features_network.pdf", width = 13.5, height = 6)
  
  layout(
    matrix(c(1, 2), nrow = 1),
    widths = c(1.35, 1.15)
  )

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Panel (a): occurrence frequencies
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  par(mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2))

  frequency_values <- rev(as.integer(variable_frequency))
  frequency_labels <- rev(unname(variable_labels))
  frequency_names <- rev(names(variable_frequency))

  x_limit <- max(frequency_values) + 3.2

  bar_positions <- barplot(
    frequency_values,
    horiz = TRUE,
    las = 1,
    col = "grey80",
    border = "grey35",
    names.arg = frequency_labels,
    xlim = c(0, x_limit),
    xlab = paste0(
      "Frequency among top ",
      top_k,
      " proxy spaces"
    ),
    main = "(a) Recurring variables"
  )

  text(
    x = frequency_values + 0.25,
    y = bar_positions,
    labels = frequency_names,
    adj = 0,
    cex = 0.62
  )

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Panel (b): network of selected proxy spaces
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  par(mar = c(1, 1, 4, 1))

  set.seed(5515L)

  network_layout <- igraph::layout_with_fr(
    proxy_graph,
    niter = 10000
  )

  plot(
    proxy_graph,
    layout = network_layout,
    vertex.size = igraph::V(proxy_graph)$size_scaled,
    vertex.label = igraph::V(proxy_graph)$label,
    vertex.label.cex = 0.85,
    vertex.label.color = "black",
    vertex.color = "grey88",
    vertex.frame.color = "grey35",
    edge.width = igraph::E(proxy_graph)$width_scaled,
    edge.color = "grey65",
    edge.curved = 0.08,
    main = "(b) Network of top proxy spaces"
  )
  
  # dev.off()
  
})
```


### Bootstrap uncertainty of predictive performance

The bootstrap resamples firms with replacement while retaining the complete time series of each selected firm. The full computation is displayed below but is not executed during rendering.

```{r}
#| label: compute-proxy-space-bootstrap
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show paired time-block bootstrap for the best proxy spaces"
#| message: false
#| warning: false

if (!requireNamespace("boot", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("The boot package is required.")
}

# ==============================================================================
# Select the best eligible pairs for the currently selected predictor
# ==============================================================================

top_k <- 30L
number_bootstrap_samples <- 1000L
bootstrap_seed <- 5515L

if (
  length(output) != nrow(pairs) ||
  length(RMSE) != nrow(pairs) ||
  length(MAE) != nrow(pairs) ||
  length(coverage) != nrow(pairs)
) {
  stop("Reload the financial results for one predictor before bootstrapping.")
}

eligible_ids <- which(
  is.finite(RMSE) &
    is.finite(MAE) &
    !is.na(coverage) &
    coverage == 1
)

eligible_ids <- eligible_ids[order(RMSE[eligible_ids])]

bootstrap_model_ids <- head(eligible_ids, top_k)
number_models <- length(bootstrap_model_ids)

if (!number_models) {
  stop("No eligible proxy spaces are available for bootstrapping.")
}

if (
  is.null(covariate_names) ||
  length(covariate_names) < max(c(pairs$i, pairs$j))
) {
  stop("The saved covariate names are missing or inconsistent with pairs.")
}

model_names <- paste0(
  covariate_names[pairs$i[bootstrap_model_ids]],
  "__",
  covariate_names[pairs$j[bootstrap_model_ids]]
)

# ==============================================================================
# Daily prediction losses, averaged over all firms
# ==============================================================================

logreturns <- as.matrix(logreturns)

if (
  !is.numeric(logreturns) ||
  any(!is.finite(logreturns)) ||
  nrow(logreturns) < 4L ||
  ncol(logreturns) < 1L
) {
  stop("Supply finite logreturns in the original time and firm order.")
}

observed_volatility <- abs(logreturns[-1L, , drop = FALSE])

T_eval <- nrow(observed_volatility)
n_eval <- ncol(observed_volatility)

# With complete, equally weighted data:
# RMSE = sqrt(mean(daily cross-sectional mean squared error)).
#
# All firms remain together at each date. Only a time x selected-model
# loss matrix is needed; no full prediction array is constructed.

loss_by_time <- vapply(
  bootstrap_model_ids,
  function(model_id) {
    h <- output[[model_id]]$sigma2_pred_S2

    if (
      !is.matrix(h) ||
      !is.numeric(h) ||
      !identical(dim(h), dim(logreturns)) ||
      any(!is.finite(h)) ||
      any(h <= 0)
    ) {
      stop(
        "Invalid conditional-variance predictions for model ",
        model_id, "."
      )
    }

    if (
      (
        !is.null(colnames(h)) &&
        !is.null(colnames(logreturns)) &&
        !identical(colnames(h), colnames(logreturns))
      ) ||
      (
        !is.null(rownames(h)) &&
        !is.null(rownames(logreturns)) &&
        !identical(rownames(h), rownames(logreturns))
      )
    ) {
      stop(
        "Prediction and observation ordering differs for model ",
        model_id, "."
      )
    }

    rowMeans(
      (
        sqrt(h[-1L, , drop = FALSE]) -
          observed_volatility
      )^2
    )
  },
  numeric(T_eval)
)

colnames(loss_by_time) <- model_names

if (any(!is.finite(loss_by_time))) {
  stop("Nonfinite prediction losses.")
}

original_rmse <- sqrt(colMeans(loss_by_time))

if (!isTRUE(all.equal(
  unname(original_rmse),
  unname(RMSE[bootstrap_model_ids]),
  tolerance = 1e-8
))) {
  stop(
    "Recomputed scores differ from the saved RMSE values. ",
    "Check the predictor, data ordering, and whether the saved ",
    "scores used sigma2_pred_S2."
  )
}

# ==============================================================================
# Paired stationary bootstrap over time
# ==============================================================================

# Starting heuristic for the mean random block length, in observation days.
# Check sensitivity to shorter and longer blocks before interpreting intervals.
mean_block_length <- as.integer(ceiling(T_eval^(1 / 3)))

set.seed(bootstrap_seed)

bootstrap_fit <- boot::tsboot(
  tseries = loss_by_time,
  statistic = function(x) {
    # Preserve a matrix even when only one model is selected.
    sqrt(colMeans(matrix(x, ncol = number_models)))
  },
  R = number_bootstrap_samples,
  l = mean_block_length,
  sim = "geom",
  parallel = "no"
)

# One multivariate call uses the same sampled time blocks for every model.
rmse_bootstrap <- bootstrap_fit$t
colnames(rmse_bootstrap) <- model_names

bootstrap_quantiles <- t(
  apply(
    rmse_bootstrap,
    2L,
    stats::quantile,
    probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
    names = FALSE
  )
)

bootstrap_summary <- data.frame(
  model_id = bootstrap_model_ids,
  variable_1 = covariate_names[pairs$i[bootstrap_model_ids]],
  variable_2 = covariate_names[pairs$j[bootstrap_model_ids]],
  predictor = predictor,
  RMSE = unname(original_rmse),
  bootstrap_SE = apply(rmse_bootstrap, 2L, stats::sd),
  lower_95 = bootstrap_quantiles[, 1L],
  upper_95 = bootstrap_quantiles[, 2L],
  row.names = NULL
)

# Pointwise percentile intervals for fixed-prediction scores.
# These exclude uncertainty from refitting, changing folds, selecting the
# best pairs, and sampling different firms. They are not simultaneous intervals.
# Interpretation requires approximately stationary, weakly dependent daily
# losses with adequate moments.

bootstrap_settings <- list(
  predictor = predictor,
  scheme = "paired stationary time-block bootstrap of daily panel losses",
  number_bootstrap_samples = number_bootstrap_samples,
  mean_block_length = mean_block_length,
  seed = bootstrap_seed,
  number_models = number_models,
  T_eval = T_eval,
  n_eval = n_eval,
  score = "sqrt(sigma2_pred_S2) versus abs(logreturns), excluding row 1",
  refitted = FALSE,
  selection_adjusted = FALSE
)

dir.create(
  "Finance_example",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

save(
  rmse_bootstrap,
  bootstrap_model_ids,
  bootstrap_summary,
  bootstrap_settings,
  file = file.path(
    "Finance_example",
    "bootstrap_rmse_results.rda"
  )
)

# Column j corresponds to bootstrap_model_ids[j], not necessarily model j.
# This file contains the bootstrap for the currently selected predictor only.
```

```{r}
#| warning: false

  "Finance_example",
  "bootstrap_rmse_results.rda"
)

if (!file.exists(bootstrap_file)) {

  )
}

}
```

### Cross-validation performance

Figure 5 shows the sorted cross-validation RMSE values and bootstrap uncertainty intervals for the 30 best-performing proxy spaces.

```{r}
#| label: fig-cross-validation-rmse
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-cap: "Cross-validation RMSE across eligible proxy spaces (upper panel) and pointwise 95% stationary-bootstrap intervals for up to 30 best-performing spaces (lower panel). Points show original CV-RMSE values. Intervals hold predictions fixed and do not adjust for proxy-space selection."
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# ==============================================================================
# Rank eligible proxy spaces for the currently selected predictor
# ==============================================================================

top_k <- 30L

eligible_ids <- which(
  is.finite(RMSE) &
    is.finite(MAE) &
    !is.na(coverage) &
    coverage == 1
)

eligible_ids <- eligible_ids[order(RMSE[eligible_ids])]

if (!length(eligible_ids)) {
  stop("No eligible proxy spaces are available for this figure.")
}

top_ids <- head(eligible_ids, top_k)
top_original_rmse <- RMSE[top_ids]
proxy_rank <- seq_along(top_ids)
sorted_rmse <- RMSE[eligible_ids]

# ==============================================================================
# Load the pre-computed bootstrap without overwriting the CV objects
# ==============================================================================

bootstrap_file <- file.path(
  "Finance_example",
  "bootstrap_rmse_results.rda"
)

if (!file.exists(bootstrap_file)) {
  stop("The pre-computed bootstrap results were not found: ", bootstrap_file)
}

bootstrap_data <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
load(bootstrap_file, envir = bootstrap_data)

required_objects <- c(
  "bootstrap_model_ids",
  "bootstrap_summary",
  "bootstrap_settings"
)

if (!all(required_objects %in% ls(bootstrap_data))) {
  stop(
    "The bootstrap file has the old structure. ",
    "Run the updated compute-proxy-space-bootstrap chunk manually."
  )
}

bootstrap_settings <- bootstrap_data$bootstrap_settings
bootstrap_summary <- bootstrap_data$bootstrap_summary
bootstrap_model_ids <- bootstrap_data$bootstrap_model_ids

if (!identical(bootstrap_settings$predictor, predictor)) {
  stop(
    "The bootstrap file contains results for ",
    bootstrap_settings$predictor,
    ", but the selected predictor is ",
    predictor,
    ". Load or compute the matching bootstrap."
  )
}

if (
  anyDuplicated(bootstrap_summary$model_id) ||
  !setequal(top_ids, bootstrap_model_ids)
) {
  stop(
    "The bootstrapped model IDs do not match the current best eligible pairs. ",
    "Regenerate the bootstrap for the current CV results."
  )
}

# Match by original model ID, not by bootstrap column position.
bootstrap_rows <- match(
  top_ids,
  bootstrap_summary$model_id
)

if (anyNA(bootstrap_rows)) {
  stop("Bootstrap summaries are missing for one or more selected models.")
}

top_bootstrap <- bootstrap_summary[
  bootstrap_rows,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

if (!isTRUE(all.equal(
  unname(top_bootstrap$RMSE),
  unname(top_original_rmse),
  tolerance = 1e-8
))) {
  stop(
    "The bootstrap and current CV scores differ. ",
    "Check that both files come from the same analysis."
  )
}

bootstrap_lower <- top_bootstrap$lower_95
bootstrap_upper <- top_bootstrap$upper_95

if (
  any(!is.finite(c(bootstrap_lower, bootstrap_upper))) ||
  any(bootstrap_lower < 0) ||
  any(bootstrap_upper < bootstrap_lower)
) {
  stop("Invalid bootstrap interval bounds.")
}

method_label <- switch(
  predictor,
  xi_blp = "Squared-innovation BLP",
  eta_gaussian = "Gaussian conditional-moment predictor"
)

# ==============================================================================
# Plot both panels and restore graphical settings
# ==============================================================================

local({
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par))

  par(
    mfrow = c(2, 1),
    mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1)
  )

  # Panel (a): all eligible proxy spaces.
  
  # pdf("rmse.pdf", width = 7, height = 5)

  plot(
    seq_along(sorted_rmse),
    sorted_rmse,
    type = "p",
    pch = 20,
    xlab = "Rank of eligible proxy space",
    ylab = "CV-RMSE",
    main = paste("(a)", method_label)
  )

  points(
    x = 1,
    y = sorted_rmse[1],
    pch = 19,

  legend(

  # dev.off()
  
  
  # Panel (b): original scores and pointwise bootstrap intervals.
  
  # pdf("bootstrap_rmse.pdf", 7, 5)
  
  plot(
    proxy_rank,
    top_original_rmse,
    type = "n",
    ylim = range(
      c(
        bootstrap_lower,
        bootstrap_upper,
        top_original_rmse
      )
    ),
    xlab = "Proxy space rank by original CV-RMSE",
    ylab = "CV-RMSE",
    main = paste0(
      "(b) Bootstrap intervals: top ",
      length(top_ids),
      " spaces"
    )
  )

  # Avoid zero-length arrows for degenerate intervals.

  if (any(nonzero_interval)) {

    lty = c(NA, 1),
    col = c("black", "grey45"),
    bty = "n",
    cex = 0.85
  )
  
  # dev.off()
  
})
```
