### Predicted volatility in the best proxy space

Figure 6 uses the best-performing proxy space.

```{r}
#| label: fig-predicted-financial-volatility
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Cross-validated conditional volatility in the best-performing financial proxy space for the selected predictor. Left: firm-level predictions (gray) and their cross-sectional median (black). Right: color indicates median predicted volatility; point size encodes its temporal standard deviation."
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# ==============================================================================
# Select the best eligible proxy space
# ==============================================================================

eligible_ids <- which(
  is.finite(RMSE) &
    is.finite(MAE) &
    !is.na(coverage) &
    coverage == 1
)

if (!length(eligible_ids)) {
  stop("No eligible proxy spaces are available for this figure.")
}

best_pair <- 781 # eligible_ids[which.min(RMSE[eligible_ids])]

best_variables <- covariate_names[
  c(
    as.integer(pairs$i[best_pair]),
    as.integer(pairs$j[best_pair])
  )
]

# ==============================================================================
# Conditional variance -> conditional standard deviation (volatility)
# ==============================================================================

predicted_variance_full <- output[[best_pair]]$sigma2_pred_S2

if (
  !is.matrix(predicted_variance_full) ||
  !is.numeric(predicted_variance_full) ||
  nrow(predicted_variance_full) < 3L ||
  any(!is.finite(predicted_variance_full)) ||
  any(predicted_variance_full <= 0)
) {
  stop("The selected model has no valid conditional-variance predictions.")
}

# Exclude initialization row 1, then take the square root.
predicted_variance_best <- predicted_variance_full[
  -1L,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

predicted_volatility <- sqrt(predicted_variance_best)

# ==============================================================================
# Align dates with the predictions
# ==============================================================================

dates_for_plot <- if (is.character(Dates)) {
  as.Date(Dates)
} else {
  Dates
}

if (length(dates_for_plot) == nrow(predicted_variance_full)) {
  # Dates already correspond to returns.
  return_dates <- dates_for_plot
} else if (
  length(dates_for_plot) == nrow(predicted_variance_full) + 1L
) {
  # Dates correspond to prices: differencing removes the first price date.
  return_dates <- dates_for_plot[-1L]
} else {
  stop(
    "Dates must contain one date per return, ",
    "or one extra initial price date."
  )
}

# Remove the date corresponding to initialization row 1.
time_vec <- return_dates[-1L]

if (
  length(time_vec) != nrow(predicted_volatility) ||
  anyNA(time_vec) ||
  is.unsorted(time_vec, strictly = TRUE)
) {
  stop("Check the date alignment and chronological ordering of predictions.")
}

# Cross-sectional median at each date.
median_vol <- apply(
  predicted_volatility,
  1L,
  stats::median
)

# Firm-specific summaries across time.
pred_vola_median <- apply(
  predicted_volatility,
  2L,
  stats::median
)

pred_vola_sd <- apply(
  predicted_volatility,
  2L,
  stats::sd
)

# ==============================================================================
# Coordinates in the selected proxy space
# ==============================================================================

if (
  length(best_variables) != 2L ||
  anyNA(best_variables) ||
  is.null(colnames(A_stand)) ||
  !all(best_variables %in% colnames(A_stand))
) {
  stop("A_stand must contain the saved variables defining the best proxy space.")
}

coords_best <- as.matrix(
  A_stand[, best_variables, drop = FALSE]
)

firm_names <- colnames(predicted_variance_full)

# Align firms explicitly when common identifiers are available.
# Otherwise A_stand must retain its original CV firm order.
if (
  !is.null(firm_names) &&
  !is.null(rownames(coords_best)) &&
  !anyDuplicated(firm_names) &&
  !anyDuplicated(rownames(coords_best)) &&
  setequal(firm_names, rownames(coords_best))
) {
  coords_best <- coords_best[firm_names, , drop = FALSE]
}

if (
  !is.numeric(coords_best) ||
  any(!is.finite(coords_best)) ||
  nrow(coords_best) != ncol(predicted_volatility)
) {
  stop("The firm coordinates and volatility predictions are incompatible.")
}

# ==============================================================================
# Colors and point sizes
# ==============================================================================

col_fun <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(
  c("steelblue", "grey", "darkred")
)

# Remove duplicate quantile boundaries when summaries are tied.
vola_breaks <- unique(
  as.numeric(
    stats::quantile(
      pred_vola_median,
      probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 8L)
    )
  )
)

if (length(vola_breaks) > 1L) {
  vola_groups <- cut(
    pred_vola_median,
    breaks = vola_breaks,
    include.lowest = TRUE,
    dig.lab = 5
  )

  vola_bins <- as.integer(vola_groups)
  legend_labels <- levels(vola_groups)
  cols <- col_fun(length(legend_labels))
} else {
  vola_bins <- rep(1L, length(pred_vola_median))
  legend_labels <- format(signif(vola_breaks, 5))
  cols <- col_fun(3L)[2L]
}

sd_range <- range(pred_vola_sd)

if (diff(sd_range) > 0) {
  scaled_cex <- sqrt(
    0.5 +
      1.5 * (pred_vola_sd - sd_range[1L]) / diff(sd_range)
  )
} else {
  scaled_cex <- rep(1, length(pred_vola_sd))
}

# ==============================================================================
# Joint figure
# ==============================================================================

local({
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par))

  par(
    mfrow = c(1, 2),
    mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1)
  )

  # Conditional volatility over time.
  
  # pdf("Pred_vola_time.pdf", width = 7, height = 5)
  
  plot(
    time_vec,
    median_vol,
    type = "n",
    ylim = range(predicted_volatility),
    xlab = "Time",
    ylab = "Predicted volatility (log-return units)",
    main = "Predicted conditional volatility"
  )

  matlines(
    time_vec,
    predicted_volatility,
    col = "lightgrey",
    lty = 1,
    lwd = 0.8
  )

  lines(
    time_vec,
    median_vol,
    col = "black",
    lwd = 2
  )
  
  # dev.off()
  
  # Firm-level volatility summaries in the proxy space.
  
  # pdf("pred_vola_space.pdf", height = 5, width = 5)
  
  plot(
    coords_best[, 1L],
    coords_best[, 2L],
    col = "grey35",
    bg = cols[vola_bins],
    pch = 21,
    cex = scaled_cex,
    lwd = 0.5,
    xlab = best_variables[1L],
    ylab = best_variables[2L],
    main = "Median predicted volatility"
  )

  legend(
    "topright",
    legend = legend_labels,
    pt.bg = cols,
    col = "grey35",
    pch = 21,
    pt.cex = 1.2,
    cex = 0.75,
    title = "Median volatility",
    bty = "n"
  )
  
  # dev.off()
  
})
```

### Full estimation in the interpretable proxy space


```{r}
#| label: compute-selected-financial-model
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show full financial estimation and parameter-surface computation"
#| message: true
#| warning: true

source("stgarch_spatial_estimation_parallelCV.R")

# ==============================================================================
# Reuse the financial CV bounds and starting values
# ==============================================================================

financial_results_file <- file.path(
  "Finance_example", "financial_proxy_space_CV_results.rds"
)

if (!file.exists(financial_results_file)) {
  stop("The financial CV results were not found: ", financial_results_file)
}

financial_fit_settings <- readRDS(financial_results_file)$settings
required_settings <- c("theta_init", "lower", "upper", "stationarity_margin")

if (!all(required_settings %in% names(financial_fit_settings))) {
  stop("The saved financial CV settings are incomplete. Regenerate the updated CV results.")
}

if (!identical(financial_fit_settings$kernel, "separable Gaussian")) {
  warning(
    "The saved CV metadata does not report a separable Gaussian kernel. ",
    "This full fit uses Gaussian weights; verify the CV kernel before comparing results."
  )
}

# ==============================================================================
# Explicitly selected financial proxy space
# ==============================================================================

# Retain the pair specified for the detailed analysis. This does not
# automatically select the best pair or use selected_id from another chunk.
selected_space_variables <- c("netIncome", "incomeTaxExpense")
 
logreturns <- as.matrix(logreturns)
A_stand <- as.matrix(A_stand)

if (is.null(colnames(A_stand)) ||
    !all(selected_space_variables %in% colnames(A_stand))) {
  stop("A_stand must contain: ", paste(selected_space_variables, collapse = ", "))
}

# Rows of A_stand must retain the firm order of the columns of logreturns.
coords_opt <- A_stand[, selected_space_variables, drop = FALSE]

if (nrow(coords_opt) != ncol(logreturns)) {
  stop("The firm coordinates and log-return columns have incompatible dimensions.")
}

local_fit_arguments <- list(
  Z = logreturns,
  coords = coords_opt,
  theta_init = financial_fit_settings$theta_init,
  lower = financial_fit_settings$lower,
  upper = financial_fit_settings$upper,
  stationarity_margin = financial_fit_settings$stationarity_margin,
  weight_function = a2d_sepgauss,
  bandwidth_function = default_bandwidth,
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_workers = 5L,
  progress = TRUE
)

# ==============================================================================
# Local GARCH estimation at all observed firms
# ==============================================================================

observed_parameter_fit <- do.call(
  fit_stgarch_local_parameters,
  c(local_fit_arguments, list(target_coords = coords_opt))
)

output_optimum_full <- observed_parameter_fit$estimated_params
b <- observed_parameter_fit$bandwidth

# Estimation failures stop inside the fitting function; failed fits are not
# replaced by zeros or accepted through an unchecked optimizer return code.

# ==============================================================================
# Fitted conditional variances and standardized innovations
# ==============================================================================

inv_return <- stgarch_invert(
  Z = logreturns,
  parameters = output_optimum_full
)

sigma2_fit <- inv_return$sigma2
volatility_fit <- sqrt(sigma2_fit)
eta_S1_hat <- inv_return$eta
xi_S1_hat <- inv_return$xi
zeta_S1_hat <- sigma2_fit * xi_S1_hat

# These are full-data fitted quantities, not cross-validated predictions.
# Row 1 initializes the filter and should be excluded from plots and scoring.

# ==============================================================================
# Innovation covariance: same estimation helper as in the corrected CV code
# ==============================================================================

D_train <- as.matrix(stats::dist(coords_opt))

par_eta_hat <- .stgarch_covariance(
  eta = eta_S1_hat[-1L, , drop = FALSE],
  D = D_train
)

covariance_estimates <- c(
  theta = par_eta_hat$range,
  sigma2 = par_eta_hat$spatial_variance,
  tau2 = par_eta_hat$nugget_variance
)

# sigma2 and tau2 are the normalized covariance components: their sum is 1.
# par_eta_hat$raw_total_variance records the pre-normalization nuisance scale.
# par_eta_hat is no longer a solnp object. No Hessian-based standard errors or
# z-statistics are calculated: this helper supplies point estimates only.

# ==============================================================================
# Local parameter surfaces on the regular grid
# ==============================================================================

grid_size <- 75L
x_vals <- seq(min(coords_opt[, 1]), max(coords_opt[, 1]), length.out = grid_size)
y_vals <- seq(min(coords_opt[, 2]), max(coords_opt[, 2]), length.out = grid_size)

grid <- expand.grid(x = x_vals, y = y_vals)
S0 <- as.matrix(grid)
n0 <- nrow(S0)

surface_bandwidth <- 0.65 # observed_parameter_fit$bandwidth

grid_parameter_fit <- do.call(
  fit_stgarch_local_parameters,
  c(
    local_fit_arguments,
    list(target_coords = S0, bandwidth = surface_bandwidth)
  )
)

estimated_params_S0 <- grid_parameter_fit$estimated_params
param_names <- c("omega", "alpha", "beta")

plot_data <- cbind(
  grid,
  as.data.frame(estimated_params_S0[, param_names, drop = FALSE])
)

coords_df <- data.frame(x = coords_opt[, 1], y = coords_opt[, 2])

# Gaussian weights allow fitting throughout the bounding rectangle, but estimates
# far from observed firms can be weakly supported. This grid is not an assertion
# of uniformly reliable interpolation over its entire extent.

# ==============================================================================
# Save the full-data estimates and plotting objects
# ==============================================================================

full_fit_settings <- list(
  theta_init = local_fit_arguments$theta_init,
  lower = local_fit_arguments$lower,
  upper = local_fit_arguments$upper,

  bandwidth_rule = "default_bandwidth",
  observed_bandwidth = b,
  surface_bandwidth = surface_bandwidth,
  grid_size = grid_size,
  covariance_normalization = "C_eta(0) = 1"
)

dir.create("Finance_example", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

save(
  selected_space_variables,
  coords_opt,
  b,
  output_optimum_full,
  sigma2_fit,
  volatility_fit,
  eta_S1_hat,
  xi_S1_hat,
  zeta_S1_hat,
  D_train,
  par_eta_hat,
  covariance_estimates,
  grid,
  S0,
  estimated_params_S0,
  param_names,
  plot_data,
  coords_df,
  surface_bandwidth,
  full_fit_settings,
  file = file.path("Finance_example", "selected_proxy_space_results.rda")
)
```

### Estimated innovation covariance

The following table reports the estimated range, spatial variance and nugget variance, together with approximate standard errors and $z$-statistics. The observed correlation range is evaluated over the pairwise distances between firms.


```{r}
#| label: selected-space-covariance-results1
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# ==============================================================================
# Estimated innovation covariance parameters
# ==============================================================================

theta_hat <- par_eta_hat$range
sigma2_hat <- par_eta_hat$spatial_variance
tau2_hat <- par_eta_hat$nugget_variance

stopifnot(
  length(theta_hat) == 1L,
  length(sigma2_hat) == 1L,
  length(tau2_hat) == 1L,
  all(is.finite(c(theta_hat, sigma2_hat, tau2_hat))),
  theta_hat > 0,
  sigma2_hat >= 0,
  tau2_hat >= 0,
  abs(sigma2_hat + tau2_hat - 1) < 1e-8
)

covariance_table <- data.frame(
  parameter = c(
    "theta",
    "sigma2",
    "tau2"
  ),
  description = c(
    "Exponential range parameter",
    "Spatial variance component (normalized)",
    "Nugget variance component (normalized)"
  ),
  estimate = c(
    theta_hat,
    sigma2_hat,
    tau2_hat
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  covariance_table,
  digits = 4,
  caption = paste(
    "Estimated standardized-innovation covariance parameters",
    "(sigma2 + tau2 = 1)."
  )
)

# ==============================================================================
# Dependence over the observed financial distances
# ==============================================================================

stopifnot(
  nrow(coords_opt) >= 2L,
  ncol(coords_opt) >= 2L,
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(coords_opt[, 1:2, drop = FALSE])))
)

# Distances between distinct firms in the selected proxy space.
observed_distances <- as.numeric(
  stats::dist(coords_opt[, 1:2, drop = FALSE])
)

# Correlations between distinct firms under the fitted model.
# The nugget contributes to marginal variance, not cross-covariance.
observed_correlations <-
  sigma2_hat * exp(-observed_distances / theta_hat) /
  (sigma2_hat + tau2_hat)

spatial_dependence_summary <- data.frame(
  quantity = c(
    "Maximum observed distance",
    "Minimum fitted correlation between firms",
    "Maximum fitted correlation between firms"
  ),
  value = c(
    max(observed_distances),
    min(observed_correlations),
    max(observed_correlations)
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  spatial_dependence_summary,
  digits = 4,
  caption = paste(
    "Pairwise distances and fitted standardized-innovation",
    "correlations in the selected financial proxy space."
  )
)
```

### Estimated GARCH parameter surfaces

The parameter surfaces are evaluated on a regular $75\times75$ grid. For the visualisation, estimates are retained only inside the convex hull of the observed firms and where the distance to the nearest firm is not unusually large.

```{r}
#| label: fig-financial-parameter-surfaces
#| layout-ncol: 3
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Estimated GARCH parameter surfaces in the selected financial proxy space. Surfaces are masked outside the observed convex hull and in regions with large nearest-firm distances; points indicate firms."
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(ggplot2)

# ==============================================================================
# Prepare the parameter-surface data
# ==============================================================================

param_names <- c("omega", "alpha", "beta")

grid_coordinates <- as.matrix(grid)
parameter_estimates <- as.matrix(estimated_params_S0)
firm_coordinates <- as.matrix(coords_opt)

stopifnot(
  ncol(grid_coordinates) == 2L,
  ncol(firm_coordinates) == 2L,
  nrow(grid_coordinates) == nrow(parameter_estimates),
  all(param_names %in% colnames(parameter_estimates)),
  all(is.finite(grid_coordinates)),
  all(is.finite(firm_coordinates))
)

parameter_estimates <- parameter_estimates[
  ,
  param_names,
  drop = FALSE
]

stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(parameter_estimates)),
  !anyDuplicated(as.data.frame(grid_coordinates))
)

# Preserve the grid order used during estimation.
plot_data <- data.frame(
  x = grid_coordinates[, 1],
  y = grid_coordinates[, 2],
  parameter_estimates,
  check.names = FALSE
)

coords_df <- data.frame(
  x = firm_coordinates[, 1],
  y = firm_coordinates[, 2]
)

axis_labels <- colnames(coords_opt)

if (is.null(axis_labels) || any(!nzchar(axis_labels))) {
  axis_labels <- selected_space_variables
}

# ==============================================================================
# Mask regions with limited spatial support
# ==============================================================================

hull_indices <- grDevices::chull(coords_df$x, coords_df$y)

if (length(hull_indices) < 3L) {
  stop("The observed firm locations do not define a two-dimensional convex hull.")
}

coords_hull <- coords_df[hull_indices, , drop = FALSE]
coords_hull <- rbind(coords_hull, coords_hull[1, , drop = FALSE])

nearest_distance <- as.numeric(
  FNN::get.knnx(
    data = as.matrix(coords_df),
    query = as.matrix(plot_data[, c("x", "y")]),
    k = 1
  )$nn.dist[, 1]
)

inside_hull <- sp::point.in.polygon(
  point.x = plot_data$x,
  point.y = plot_data$y,
  pol.x = coords_hull$x,
  pol.y = coords_hull$y
) > 0

# Retain the existing distance-based plotting heuristic.
distance_threshold <- grDevices::boxplot.stats(
  nearest_distance
)$stats[5]

plot_data$use <-
  inside_hull &
  is.finite(nearest_distance) &
  nearest_distance <= distance_threshold

if (!any(plot_data$use)) {
  stop("No grid points remain after applying the spatial plotting mask.")
}

for (param in param_names) {
  plot_data[[paste0(param, "_masked")]] <- ifelse(
    plot_data$use,
    plot_data[[param]],
    NA_real_
  )
}

# ==============================================================================
# Construct and save the parameter-surface plots
# ==============================================================================

col_vals <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(
  c("steelblue", "grey", "darkred")
)(100)

# Display the parameters in the order used in the paper.
for (param in c("beta", "alpha", "omega")) {

  # Use one explicit plotting column for each panel.
  panel_data <- plot_data
  panel_data$fill_value <- panel_data[[paste0(param, "_masked")]]

  gg <- ggplot(
    panel_data,
    aes(x = x, y = y)
  ) +
    geom_raster(
      aes(fill = fill_value),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

  # Constant surfaces do not have meaningful contour levels.
  finite_values <- panel_data$fill_value[
    is.finite(panel_data$fill_value)
  ]

  if (length(unique(finite_values)) > 1L) {
    gg <- gg +
      geom_contour(
        aes(z = fill_value),
        colour = "black",
        linewidth = 0.3,
        bins = 10,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
  }

  gg <- gg +
    geom_point(
      data = coords_df,
      aes(x = x, y = y),
      colour = "black",
      fill = "white",
      shape = 21,
      size = 2,
      stroke = 0.3,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colours = col_vals,
      na.value = "transparent",
      name = param
    ) +
    coord_fixed() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Estimated", param),
      x = axis_labels[1],
      y = axis_labels[2]
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

  print(gg)

  ggsave(
    filename = paste0("surface_", param, ".pdf"),
    plot = gg,
    width = 5,
    height = 5,
    units = "in"
  )
}
```

## PM10 residual volatility in Italy

The second empirical application analyses the residuals from a fitted spatiotemporal PM$_{10}$ mean model. Residual volatility is interpreted as time-varying model uncertainty after the systematic mean structure has been removed.

Stations with more than 20% missing residuals are excluded. The remaining missing values are imputed by centred Gaussian draws with standard deviation equal to the empirical standard deviation of the observed residuals. Predictive performance is evaluated by five-fold spatial cross-validation, leaving out complete monitoring locations.

### Data preparation

```{r}
#| label: prepare-pm10-data
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show PM10 data-preparation code"
#| results: hide
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(progress)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

# ==============================================================================
# Load and prepare the PM10 residual data
# ==============================================================================

lssrm_residuals <- read.csv(
  "LRSSM_Residuals/residuals_PM10_rankR100.csv"
)

coords <- read.csv(
  "LRSSM_Residuals/points_train.csv"
)

timestamps <- read.csv(
  "LRSSM_Residuals/timestamp.csv"
)

timestamps <- as.Date(timestamps[, 1])

# The residual matrix initially has locations in rows and time in columns.
# Transpose it to the convention T x n.
Z <- t(
  as.matrix(lssrm_residuals)
)

coords <- as.matrix(coords)

# Restrict the analysis to the first 1,250 daily observations.
Z <- Z[1:1250, ]
timestamps <- timestamps[1:1250]

T <- nrow(Z)
n <- ncol(Z)

# Proportion of missing residuals at each monitoring station.
na_prop <- colMeans(
  is.na(Z)
)

# Retain stations with no more than 20% missing residuals.
keep <- na_prop <= 0.20

n_removed <- sum(!keep)
n_retained <- sum(keep)

Z <- Z[
  ,
  keep,
  drop = FALSE
]

coords <- coords[
  keep,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Update dimensions after removing stations.
T <- nrow(Z)
n <- ncol(Z)

# Impute the remaining missing values using the original procedure.
Z[is.na(Z)] <- rnorm(
  sum(is.na(Z)),
  mean = 0,
  sd = sd(
    Z,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(coords) == n
)

# Model settings.
b <- 0.8
p <- 1

theta_init <- c(
  0.3,
  0.2,
  0.3
)

lb <- c(
  1e-10,
  0,
  0
)

ub <- c(
  Inf,
  0.999,
  0.999
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pm10-data-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the PM10 residual data used in the volatility analysis."
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

pm10_data_summary <- data.frame(
  quantity = c(
    "Daily observations",
    "Original monitoring stations",
    "Removed monitoring stations",
    "Retained monitoring stations",
    "Maximum permitted missingness"
  ),
  value = c(
    T,
    length(keep),
    n_removed,
    n_retained,
    "20%"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  pm10_data_summary,
  align = c("l", "r")
)
```

### Five-fold spatial cross-validation

The complete cross-validation is computationally intensive. The code is included for reproducibility but is not executed when the Quarto document is rendered. Instead, the subsequent chunk loads the pre-computed predictions.


```{r}
#| label: compute-pm10-spatial-cross-validation
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show PM10 spatial cross-validation computation"

source("stgarch_spatial_estimation_parallelCV.R")

# Z contains the mean-adjusted PM10 residuals.
stopifnot(all(is.finite(Z)))

site_second_moments <- colMeans(Z^2)

if (any(!is.finite(site_second_moments)) ||
    any(site_second_moments <= 0)) {
  stop("Check for degenerate or invalid residual series.")
}

v_ref <- median(site_second_moments)

lb <- c(
  omega = 1e-8 * v_ref,
  alpha = 0,
  beta  = 0
)

ub <- c(
  omega = 10 * max(site_second_moments),
  alpha = 1,
  beta  = 1
)

# Initial persistence = 0.95 and initial unconditional variance = v_ref.
theta_init <- c(
  omega = 0.05 * v_ref,
  alpha = 0.05,
  beta  = 0.90
)


# Use identical folds for both prediction methods.
set.seed(5515L)

folds_pm10 <- sample(
  rep(
    seq_len(5L),
    length.out = ncol(Z)
  )
)

common_arguments <- list(
  Z = Z,
  coords = coords,
  theta_init = theta_init,
  lower = lb,
  upper = ub,

  # Compact, smooth spatial kernel.
  weight_function = stgarch_weights,
  bandwidth_function = stgarch_bandwidth,

  # Enforce alpha + beta <= 1 - stationarity_margin.
  stationarity_margin = 1e-4,

  # Applied to the squared-process prediction for xi-BLP only.
  epsilon = 1e-8,

  folds = folds_pm10,
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_workers = 5L,
  progress = TRUE
)

fit_xi <- do.call(
  fit_stgarch_spatial_cv,
  c(
    common_arguments,
    list(predictor = "xi_blp")
  )
)

fit_eta <- do.call(
  fit_stgarch_spatial_cv,
  c(
    common_arguments,
    list(predictor = "eta_gaussian")
  )
)

comparison_pm10 <- data.frame(
  predictor = c("xi_blp", "eta_gaussian"),
  RMSE = c(fit_xi$RMSE_vol, fit_eta$RMSE_vol),
  MAE = c(fit_xi$MAE_vol, fit_eta$MAE_vol),
  coverage = c(
    fit_xi$evaluation_coverage,
    fit_eta$evaluation_coverage
  )
)

print(comparison_pm10)

results_directory <- "LRSSM_Residuals"

dir.create(
  results_directory,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

pm10_results_file <- file.path(
  results_directory,
  "PM10_STGARCH_spatial_CV.rds"
)

saveRDS(
  list(
    fit_xi = fit_xi,
    fit_eta = fit_eta,
    comparison = comparison_pm10,
    folds = folds_pm10
  ),
  file = pm10_results_file
)
```

### Predicted residual volatility

The spatial panel displays the median cross-validated volatility prediction at
each monitoring station. Point size represents temporal variability in the
prediction. The temporal panel shows the cross-sectional median and
interquartile range together with two selected monitoring stations.

```{r}
#| label: fig-pm10-predicted-volatility

#| fig-height: 5.5

  cex = 0.8
)

# dev.off()


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Panel (b): temporal evolution
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

par(
  mar = c(
    4.2,
    4.2,
    3.2,
    1.2
  )
)

# pdf("Pred_vola_time_lrssm.pdf", width = 7, height = 5)

plot(
  time_vec,
  median_vol,
  type = "n",
  ylim = range(
    c(
      lower_vol,
      upper_vol,
      Z_pred[, idx_low],
      Z_pred[, idx_high]
    ),
    na.rm = TRUE
  ),
  xlab = "Time",
  ylab = "Predicted volatility",
  main = "Predicted volatility over time"
)

polygon(
  c(
    time_vec,
    rev(time_vec)
  ),
  c(
    lower_vol,
    rev(upper_vol)
  ),
  col = "grey85",
  border = NA
)

lines(
  time_vec,
  Z_pred[, idx_low],
  col = col_low,
  lwd = 1.4
)

lines(
  time_vec,
  Z_pred[, idx_high],
  col = col_high,
  lwd = 1.4
)

lines(
  time_vec,
  median_vol,
  col = "black",
  lwd = 2
)

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = c(
    "Median",
    "Interquartile range",
    "Low-volatility station",
    "High-volatility station"
  ),
  col = c(
    "black",
    "grey85",
    col_low,
    col_high
  ),
  lwd = c(
    2,
    8,
    1.4,
    1.4
  ),
  lty = 1,
  bty = "n",
  cex = 0.8
)

# dev.off()

layout(1)
par(old_par)
```

### Full estimation and spatial parameter surfaces

The model is next re-estimated using all retained monitoring stations.
The local GARCH parameters are evaluated at the centroids of a hexagonal
tessellation of Italy. The full computation is displayed but not executed
during rendering.

```{r}
#| label: compute-pm10-full-model
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show full PM10 estimation and surface code"
#| message: true
#| warning: true

source("stgarch_spatial_estimation_parallelCV.R")

# Use the same parameter bounds and kernel specification as in the CV analysis.
# lb and ub must be finite; theta_init must be strictly inside the constraints.
local_fit_arguments <- list(
  Z = Z,
  coords = coords,
  theta_init = theta_init,
  lower = lb,
  upper = ub,
  weight_function = stgarch_weights,
  bandwidth_function = stgarch_bandwidth,
  stationarity_margin = 1e-4,
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_workers = 5L,
  progress = TRUE
)

# ==============================================================================
# Full estimation at the observed monitoring stations
# ==============================================================================

observed_parameter_fit <- do.call(
  fit_stgarch_local_parameters,
  c(local_fit_arguments, list(target_coords = coords))
)

output_optimum_full <- observed_parameter_fit$estimated_params
b <- observed_parameter_fit$bandwidth

# Failed optimizations stop inside the fitting function; there is no longer
# a separate observed_parameter_fit$convergence object.

# ==============================================================================
# Recover the fitted variance and innovation processes
# ==============================================================================

inv_return <- stgarch_invert(
  Z = Z,
  parameters = output_optimum_full
)

sigma2_fit <- inv_return$sigma2
eta_S1_hat <- inv_return$eta
xi_S1_hat <- inv_return$xi
zeta_S1_hat <- sigma2_fit * xi_S1_hat

# Row 1 initializes the filter and is excluded from covariance estimation.
eta_train <- eta_S1_hat[-1L, , drop = FALSE]
D_train <- as.matrix(stats::dist(coords))

# ==============================================================================
# Fit exactly the same spatial covariance model as in cross-validation
# ==============================================================================

# This helper is defined in the sourced estimation file and used by the CV
# function. It fits the covariance and normalizes it to C_eta(0) = 1.
par_eta_hat <- .stgarch_covariance(
  eta = eta_train,
  D = D_train
)

# Keep these names for downstream tables. sigma2 and tau2 now denote the
# normalized covariance components, so sigma2 + tau2 = 1.
theta <- par_eta_hat$range
sigma2 <- par_eta_hat$spatial_variance
tau2 <- par_eta_hat$nugget_variance

# par_eta_hat is now the covariance helper's result, not an optim object.
# Its raw_total_variance field records the scale before normalization.
# The old numerical Hessian is not calculated or saved.

# ==============================================================================
# Construct a hexagonal parameter-estimation grid over Italy
# ==============================================================================

italy <- sf::st_read("LRSSM_Residuals/it_shp/it.shp", quiet = TRUE)
italy <- sf::st_make_valid(italy)
italy_proj <- sf::st_transform(italy, 3035)

cell_size <- 25000

hex_grid <- sf::st_make_grid(
  italy_proj,
  cellsize = cell_size,
  square = FALSE
)

hex_grid <- sf::st_sf(
  grid_id = seq_along(hex_grid),
  geometry = hex_grid
)

hex_italy <- sf::st_intersection(
  hex_grid,
  sf::st_union(italy_proj)
)

# Construct centroids in the projected CRS, then transform to the same
# longitude/latitude coordinates used by the monitoring-station model.
# This assumes coords[, 1:2] are longitude/latitude in EPSG:4326.
centroids_hex <- sf::st_sf(
  grid_id = hex_italy$grid_id,
  geometry = sf::st_centroid(sf::st_geometry(hex_italy))
)
centroids_hex <- sf::st_transform(centroids_hex, 4326)
S0 <- sf::st_coordinates(centroids_hex)[, 1:2, drop = FALSE]
n0 <- nrow(S0)

# ==============================================================================
# Estimate parameter surfaces where the spatial kernel has training support
# ==============================================================================

grid_supported <- vapply(seq_len(n0), function(i) {
  w <- local_fit_arguments$weight_function(
    coords[, 1] - S0[i, 1],
    coords[, 2] - S0[i, 2],
    b
  )
  any(w > 0)
}, logical(1))

if (!any(grid_supported)) {
  stop("No grid centroids have kernel support; check coordinates and bandwidth.")
}

message(
  "Estimating ", sum(grid_supported), " of ", n0, " grid cells; ",
  sum(!grid_supported), " cells have no kernel support and remain NA."
)

grid_parameter_fit <- do.call(
  fit_stgarch_local_parameters,
  c(
    local_fit_arguments,
    list(
      target_coords = S0[grid_supported, , drop = FALSE],
      bandwidth = b
    )
  )
)

param_names <- c("omega", "alpha", "beta")
estimated_params_S0 <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n0,
  ncol = length(param_names),
  dimnames = list(NULL, param_names)
)
estimated_params_S0[grid_supported, ] <- grid_parameter_fit$estimated_params

# Preserve every grid row and its geometry. Unsupported cells remain NA;
# this support mask does not represent a confidence or precision criterion.
grid_plot <- hex_italy
grid_plot$kernel_supported <- grid_supported
for (param in param_names) {
  grid_plot[[param]] <- estimated_params_S0[, param]
  grid_plot[[paste0(param, "_masked")]] <- estimated_params_S0[, param]
}

# coords_sf contains MONITORING STATIONS, not grid centroids.
coords_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(
  data.frame(
    station_id = seq_len(nrow(coords)),
    lon = coords[, 1],
    lat = coords[, 2]
  ),
  coords = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE
)
coords_sf <- sf::st_transform(coords_sf, sf::st_crs(grid_plot))

# ==============================================================================
# Save the pre-computed full-model results
# ==============================================================================

results_directory <- "LRSSM_Residuals"
dir.create(results_directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

saveRDS(
  list(
    output_optimum_full = output_optimum_full,
    sigma2_fit = sigma2_fit,
    eta_S1_hat = eta_S1_hat,
    xi_S1_hat = xi_S1_hat,
    zeta_S1_hat = zeta_S1_hat,
    D_train = D_train,
    par_eta_hat = par_eta_hat,
    theta = theta,
    sigma2 = sigma2,
    tau2 = tau2,
    estimated_params_S0 = estimated_params_S0,
    grid_plot = grid_plot,
    coords_sf = coords_sf,
    centroids_hex = centroids_hex,
    S0 = S0,
    grid_supported = grid_supported,
    param_names = param_names,
    bandwidth = b,
    cell_size = cell_size,
    fitting_settings = list(
      theta_init = theta_init,
      lower = lb,
      upper = ub,
      stationarity_margin = local_fit_arguments$stationarity_margin,
      kernel = "separable biweight"
    )
  ),
  file = file.path(results_directory, "LRSSM_STGARCH_full_results.rds")
)
```


### Spatially varying GARCH parameters


```{r}
#| label: fig-pm10-parameter-surfaces
#| layout-ncol: 3
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Estimated spatially varying GARCH parameter surfaces for the PM10 residual volatility model. Cells without spatial kernel support are left unfilled."
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(ggplot2)

# Load the results produced by the updated full-estimation block.
full_results_file <- file.path(
  "LRSSM_Residuals",
  "LRSSM_STGARCH_full_results.rds"
)


full_results <- readRDS(full_results_file)

grid_plot <- full_results$grid_plot
coords_sf <- full_results$coords_sf

param_names <- c("omega", "alpha", "beta")

if (
  !is.logical(grid_plot$kernel_supported) ||
  anyNA(grid_plot$kernel_supported)
) {
  stop("The saved kernel-support mask is invalid.")
}

if (
  is.na(sf::st_crs(grid_plot)) ||
  is.na(sf::st_crs(coords_sf))
) {
  stop("Both the grid and monitoring stations need a valid CRS.")
}

# Monitoring stations and grid must use the same plotting CRS.
coords_sf_plot <- sf::st_transform(
  coords_sf,
  sf::st_crs(grid_plot)
)

col_vals <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(
  c("steelblue", "grey", "darkred")
)(100)

for (param in param_names) {

  plot_data <- grid_plot

  plot_data$fill_value <- ifelse(
    plot_data$kernel_supported,
    plot_data[[param]],
    NA_real_
  )

  if (!any(is.finite(plot_data$fill_value))) {
    stop("No finite supported estimates are available for ", param, ".")
  }

  gg <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(
      data = plot_data,
      aes(fill = fill_value),
      colour = NA
    ) +
    geom_sf(
      data = plot_data,
      fill = NA,
      colour = "grey70",
      linewidth = 0.05
    ) +
    geom_sf(
      data = coords_sf_plot,
      colour = "black",
      fill = "white",
      shape = 21,
      size = 1.5,
      stroke = 0.3
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colours = col_vals,
      na.value = "transparent",
      name = param
    ) +
    coord_sf() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Estimated", param),
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # pdf_file <- paste0("surface_", param, "_lssrm.pdf")
  # ggsave(pdf_file, plot = gg, width = 5, height = 6)

  print(gg)
}
```
